requirements/2x2-photo.h1: 2×2 Photo Requirements in 2026: a Complete US Guide to Avoid Rejections

sections.title: 2×2 Photo Requirements in 2026: a Complete US Guide to Avoid Rejections
items: Planning to apply for a U.S. ID that requires a 2x2 (51×51 mm / 600 x 600-pixel) photo? Find out about this photo format — which US documents require it, universal content rules, document-specific digital upload specifications, and the critical December 2025 USCIS policy change. Information in this Guide is based strictly on travel.state.gov , uscis.gov , and other official sources. If your form asks for the smaller square instead, you can make a 1x1 picture size online with our editor.

The 2×2 inch (51×51 mm) square photo is the standard US government ID photo format, used for passports, visas, and most immigration documents. Despite the single print size, digital upload requirements differ significantly by document type — and as of December 12, 2025, USCIS no longer requires photos submitted with most immigration forms. Outside government forms the same square is used too, and the page for a resume photo 2x2 inches covers that case.

sections.title: What Is a 2×2 Inch Photo?
items: A 2×2 inch photo is a square photograph measuring exactly 2 inches wide by 2 inches tall — equivalent to 51×51 mm or 5.08×5.08 cm. It has a 1:1 aspect ratio. This is the standard format for all official US government identity document photos issued by the U.S. Department of State (passports and visas) and the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Both follow the official biometric standard of the International Civil Aviation Organization Document 9303 , but with a country-specific 2x2-inch ID photo size. The 35x45 mm photo size is used for passports, Schengen visas, and ID cards, and our separate page prepares it from a phone shot.

The square format is specific to the United States and a small number of other countries. Within the 2×2-inch frame, your head must occupy a specific portion of the image. For US passport photos, the head must measure between 1 and 1⅜ inches (25–35 mm) from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head. For USCIS immigration documents, the head should cover 50–69% of the photo height from chin to crown. Most other countries use rectangular formats, and you can prepare a 3x4 cm photo size online on a separate page.

sections.title: Which US Documents Require a 2×2 Photo?
items: The 2×2-inch format is required for the following US government documents. Each is administered by a different agency with its own photo submission workflow.
Document / Form
Issuing Agency & Photo Submission Method
US Passport (new application or renewal by mail)
US Department of State — 1 printed 2×2 photo submitted with paper form DS-11 or DS-82
US Passport (online renewal)
US Department of State — digital photo uploaded at opr.travel.state.gov ; no print required
US Nonimmigrant Visa (DS-160)
US Department of State — digital photo uploaded in DS-160 form; printed photo required at interview at some embassies
US Immigrant Visa (DS-260)
US Department of State — digital photo uploaded in DS-260 form
Diversity Visa Lottery (DV Program)
US Department of State — digital photo uploaded at dvprogram.state.gov
Green Card — Adjustment of Status (I-485)
USCIS — photo taken at ASC biometric appointment since December 12, 2025. Do NOT submit photos with the form.
Naturalization (N-400)
USCIS — photo taken at ASC biometric appointment since December 12, 2025. Do NOT submit photos with the form.
Employment Authorization (I-765 / EAD)
USCIS — photo taken at ASC biometric appointment since December 12, 2025. Do NOT submit photos with the form.
Permanent Resident Card Renewal (I-90)
USCIS — photo taken at ASC biometric appointment since December 12, 2025. Do NOT submit photos with the form.
Travel Document / Advance Parole (I-131)
USCIS — check current online instructions at uscis.gov ; policy may vary by form version
Certificate of Citizenship (N-600)
USCIS — photo taken at ASC since December 12, 2025. Do NOT submit photos with the form.
Refugee Travel Document
USCIS — 2 printed 2×2 photos required. Check current form instructions at uscis.gov .
Visa application interview (in-person at US embassy or consulate)
US Department of State — printed 2×2 photos may be required at the interview window. Check the specific embassy's requirements.

sections.title: Critical: USCIS Photo Policy Change — December 12, 2025
items: As of December 12, 2025, USCIS no longer accepts photos submitted with Form I-485, I-765, N-400, I-90, I-131, N-600, or most other forms requiring biometric processing. Many printed form instructions still say to include two passport-style photos — those instructions are outdated. Follow only the current online instructions at uscis.gov , not the printed form.

USCIS Policy Announcement PA-2025-29, effective December 12, 2025, centralized photo capture to Application Support Center (ASC) biometric appointments. When you file most USCIS forms, you will receive a biometric appointment notice. At that appointment, USCIS staff take your fingerprints, signature, and photograph using their own biometric equipment. You do not supply a photo.
If you include photos with a form that no longer requires them, USCIS will not return the photos and will not use them. Including them does not improve your application and may cause confusion.
Forms where photos are NO LONGER submitted with the form (since December 12, 2025)
Form I-485 — Adjustment of Status (Green Card)
Form N-400 — Application for Naturalization
Form I-765 — Employment Authorization Document
Form I-90 — Renewal of Permanent Resident Card
Form I-131 — Application for Travel Document (check specific instructions)
Form N-600 — Certificate of Citizenship
Forms where printed 2×2 photos may still be required
Refugee Travel Document — check current uscis.gov instructions before filing
In-person visa interviews at US embassies and consulates abroad — the embassy or consulate may request printed photos at the counter; check the specific post's requirements
Green card interview at USCIS field office — some applicants are asked to bring 2 photos

The USCIS policy change affects form submission only. The photo itself — when captured at the ASC — still follows the same 2×2 format biometric standards. The only thing that changed is who takes the photo and when.

sections.title: Universal 2×2 Photo Requirements: All US Documents
items: The following requirements apply to every US government 2×2 photo, regardless of which document it is for. These are not negotiable and do not vary by agency.
Requirement
Specification
1. Print size
2×2 inches (51×51 mm) — square format, 1:1 aspect ratio
2. Color
Full color — no black-and-white photos
3. Recency
Taken within the last 6 months, reflecting current appearance
4. Background
Plain white or off-white — no shadows, patterns, textures, lines, or objects
5. Head size and position
1-1 ⅜ inches. Facing the camera directly, full face in view, no tilt or rotation
6. Eyes
Both eyes fully open, directed at the camera, not obstructed by hair
7. Expression
Neutral facial expression. Natural smile permitted for passports (mouth closed). Neutral required for visa applications.
8. Glasses
Not permitted — must be removed. Medical exception: signed doctor's note.
9. Head coverings
Not permitted. Religious exception: signed statement. Medical exception: signed doctor's note. Full face must be visible.
10. Uniforms / camouflage
Not permitted
11. Headphones / devices
Not permitted
12. Face coverings / masks
Not permitted — full face must be visible
13. Digital editing / AI
Not permitted. No filters, retouching, AI enhancement, or AI-generated images.
14. Print quality
Matte or glossy photo-quality paper. Not photocopied, not scanned, not damaged.

sections.title: Head Size Requirements: Passport vs. USCIS — The Key Difference
items: The only substantive content difference between a passport photo and a USCIS immigration photo is the head size specification. Both use 2×2 inch prints, but the agencies define head coverage differently:
Agency / Document
Head Size Requirement
US Passport (State Dept)
1 to 1⅜ inches (25–35 mm) from bottom of chin to top of head
US Visa (State Dept)
Same as passport: 1 to 1⅜ inches (25–35 mm)
USCIS immigration documents
Head covers 50–69% of the photo height from chin to crown

In practice, these two specifications are very similar and produce visually identical results. A photo prepared to the passport head-size standard (1 to 1⅜ inches) will generally also meet the USCIS 50–69% range. A photo where the head is too small (below 1 inch / 25mm) or too large (above 1⅜ inches / 35mm) will fail both standards.

The visa digital upload limit of 240 KB is very strict. A standard phone photo is 3–10 MB is over 40 times the limit! You must compress the JPEG before uploading to DS-160. Export at quality 70–80%, and always use a reliable visa photo maker to turn your photo into the official ID image before submitting.

sections.title: 2×2 Pixel Equivalent: What 2×2 Inches Means Digitally
items: The 2×2 inch print size translates to different pixel counts depending on resolution (DPI — dots per inch):
Resolution
Pixel dimensions for a 2×2-inch print
300 DPI (print standard)
600 × 600 pixels
600 DPI

The U.S. Department of State visa digital upload portal requires exactly 600×600 to 1,200×1,200 pixels — corresponding to a 2×2-inch print at 300 to 600 DPI. For the online passport renewal portal, the same pixel range applies: 600×600 minimum, 1,200×1,200 maximum. DPI does not matter for screen display or digital upload — only pixel count matters. A 600×600 pixel image is a 600×600 pixel image regardless of what DPI metadata is embedded in the file. What DPI metadata controls is only how the image is sized when printed. For digital submission, focus on pixel dimensions and file size, not dots per inch.

sections.title: How to Take a Compliant 2×2 ID Photo at Home
items: Whether you are taking the photo for a passport, visa, or any other document using the 2×2 format, the setup process is identical. The content requirements are the same; only the digital file specifications at upload differ by portal. The same setup works for other square formats: you can crop a 4x4 photo size online from the same source picture.

sections.title: Setup
items: Find a smooth, flat white or off-white wall, or tape a sheet of white foam board or white poster paper against any surface. The background must be one solid, uniform color with no shadows or textures.
Stand 3–4 feet (1 meter) away from the background wall. This distance prevents your body from casting a shadow onto the background behind you.

Position yourself facing a large window (window in front of you, not behind) for natural, even lighting, or use two lamps at 45-degree angles on either side of your camera position. Lighting must be even on both sides of your face.

sections.title: Camera Settings
items: Use your phone's rear camera — not the front-facing camera. Rear cameras capture at 36–48 MP without automatic AI processing. Front cameras capture at 12 MP with automatic beauty enhancement enabled by default.
Turn off all AI enhancement, Portrait mode, Beauty mode, Scene Optimizer, Smart HDR, and any skin-smoothing feature before taking the photo. These alterations will cause rejection.
Do not use digital zoom. Zoom creates pixelation. Move the camera closer instead.

sections.title: Framing and Position
items: The bottom of the frame should be at your shoulders — at the point where your neck meets your shoulders. This gives the correct head-and-shoulders framing.
Your face should be centered in the frame. Face the camera directly — both ears at equal height, head not tilted, not rotated to the side.
Both eyes must be fully open and visible. Clear any hair from your eyes before shooting.
Remove glasses, hats, headphones, and face coverings before the photo.
Neutral expression or natural smile (mouth closed). Eyes open.

sections.title: Export and File Preparation
items: Take the photo with your phone's rear camera. Transfer the original file by cable, AirDrop, or cloud sync — never via text message (which compresses the image).
Do not open the file in any editing app. Do not crop, filter, adjust brightness, or apply any change. Use the upload portal's built-in cropping tool for any needed adjustments.
For visa DS-160 upload (max 240 KB): export as JPEG at quality 70–75. A head-and-shoulders crop at 600×600 pixels at JPEG quality 75 produces a file of approximately 40–100 KB.
For passport online renewal upload (max 10 MB): standard JPEG export at quality 85–90 is typically well within the limit.
Verify: file is square (equal width and height), format is JPEG (or HEIF for passport portal), and file size is within the range for your specific portal.

sections.title: Where to Get a 2×2 Photo in the United States
Commercial Photo Studios, Pharmacies, Post Offices
items: CVS, Walgreens, Walmart Photo, Costco Photo, and most FedEx Office and UPS Store locations offer passport photo services. The standard cost is $10–$20 for 2 printed photos. These services use calibrated photo equipment and trained staff. The printed photos are ready in minutes and are compliant with the US government 2×2 standards when done correctly. Always confirm the service uses a white background and takes the photo at the current session — not from a file on your phone.

sections.title: Acceptance Facilities
items: US passport acceptance facilities (post offices, libraries, and government offices listed at iafdb.travel.state.gov ) often provide photo services as part of the passport application process. Some charge separately for the photo; others include it in the application fee.

sections.title: Take a Photo at Home and Use an Online Passport Photo Maker
items: Any modern smartphone camera produces sufficient resolution for a compliant 2×2 photo. Set your phone to the highest quality setting, disable portrait mode and all beauty or AI enhancement features, and have another person take the shot. Stand in front of a plain white wall with even natural light on your face — no shadows, no overhead lighting. Look straight at the camera with a neutral expression and both eyes fully open.

Once the photo is taken, use the PhotoGov US passport photo editor to crop, resize, and adjust the background to the official 2×2 standard. PhotoGov processes only the technical parameters of your image and does not alter your face or skin tone. An optional attire adjustment is available if your clothing does not meet formal submission requirements. For extra assurance, the Human Verification option lets a PhotoGov specialist review your photo and provide a personal compliance assessment before you submit.

If you only need to crop and check proportions, the State Department's official Photo Tool handles basic resizing to the 2×2 format. For official USCIS photo specifications, refer to the USCIS Photo Requirements page.

sections.title: What Cannot Be Used as a 2×2 US ID Photo
items: Driver's license photo: The 2×2 format is not used for US driver's licenses. Driver's licenses use a different aspect ratio defined by each state's DMV, and the DMV takes the photo in-office. A driver's license photo cannot be used for a passport or visa application.

LinkedIn or professional headshot: Professional headshots use different framing, backgrounds (including gray and non-white), and often involve AI enhancement or retouching — all of which are prohibited for government 2×2 photos.

REAL ID photo: REAL ID uses the same in-office DMV photo process as a standard driver's license. It is not the same format as a passport photo and cannot be submitted for passport or visa applications.
Cropped group photo: Any photo where another person's shoulder, arm, or any part of another person is visible is grounds for automatic rejection.

Screenshot of another photo: Photographing a photo displayed on a screen, or screenshotting a passport photo from a website or app, produces an image of insufficient quality and is specifically prohibited.
Photo older than 6 months: The photo must reflect your current appearance. A photo more than 6 months old, or one that no longer resembles you, will be rejected.

AI-generated images: Photos created by AI image generators or AI photo services are explicitly banned by both the State Department (since 2024, expanded in 2026) and USCIS. Pixel-level forensic detection is used during review.

sections.title: When You Need a New 2×2 Photo After an Appearance Change
items: Your 2×2 photo must match your current appearance. Minor changes — growing a beard, coloring your hair, normal aging — do not require a new passport. Major changes do. The State Department defines these thresholds:

sections.title: Minor Changes — New Photo Not Required
items: Growing or removing a beard or mustache
Coloring or changing hairstyle
Normal aging process
Weight changes within a normal range

sections.title: Major Changes — New Passport Application Required
items: Significant facial surgery or trauma
Adding or removing numerous large facial piercings or tattoos
Significant weight loss or gain that substantially alters facial appearance

For immigration documents, USCIS applies a similar standard — your photo must be recognizably you. If your appearance has changed significantly since your last USCIS photo on file, request updated biometrics at your next USCIS interaction.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
Can I Use the Same Photo for My US Passport and Visa?
items: No. Though the same printed 2×2 photo meets the content requirements for both, the digital upload specifications differ: the passport online renewal portal accepts files up to 10 MB in JPG/JPEG/HEIF format, while the visa DS-160 portal requires JPEG only and a maximum file size of 240 KB. Use the same original photo, but export two different digital files with different compression settings for each portal.

sections.title: Is 2×2 the Same as 51×51 mm?
items: Yes. 2 inches = 50.8 mm, which rounds to 51 mm. The formats are functionally identical. The State Department and USCIS specify 2×2 inches (51×51 mm). A photo printed at exactly 51×51 mm is compliant.

sections.title: Can I Print a 2×2 Photo at Home?
items: Yes, if you have a photo-quality printer and matte or glossy photo paper. Standard office paper and inkjet prints on plain paper are not acceptable — the State Department requires 'matte or glossy photo quality paper.' Most home inkjet printers on photo paper produce acceptable quality for passport and visa photos. Verify the print size is exactly 2×2 inches before submitting.

sections.title: My Ds-160 Visa Photo Upload Keeps Failing. What is The Problem?
items: The DS-160 portal has the strictest file size limit of any US government photo portal: 240 KB maximum. Most phone photos are 3–10 MB, which is 12–40 times too large. Export your photo as a JPEG at quality 70–75 and verify the file size before attempting another upload. The image must also be square (equal width and height), in JPEG format specifically (not PNG or HEIF), and between 600×600 and 1,200×1,200 pixels.

sections.title: Do I Still Need to Submit Photos With My USCIS Immigration Forms?
items: For most USCIS forms — including I-485, N-400, I-765, I-90, and N-600 — no. Since December 12, 2025, USCIS takes your photo at the ASC biometric appointment. Do not submit photos with these forms, even if the printed form instructions tell you to. The printed instructions have not been updated. Follow the current online instructions at uscis.gov only.

sections.title: What Pixel Dimensions Should I Use for a 2×2 Photo?
items: For print: a 2×2 inch photo at 300 DPI = 600×600 pixels; at 600 DPI = 1,200×1,200 pixels. For digital upload: the State Department requires 600×600 to 1,200×1,200 pixels for both passport and visa portals. The image must be perfectly square — width and height must be identical. A 601×600 image will be rejected.

sections.title: Can I Smile in My 2×2 ID Photo?
items: For US passports: yes. The State Department permits a natural smile with the mouth closed. For US visa applications (DS-160): a neutral expression is generally required or strongly preferred. For USCIS biometric photos taken at the ASC: the biometric officer will instruct you on expression — typically neutral. Check the specific agency's current guidance for each document type.

sections.title: What if I Always Wear Glasses? Can I Wear Them In My 2×2 Photo?
items: No. Glasses have been prohibited in US government 2×2 photos since November 2016. This applies to prescription glasses, reading glasses, and all corrective eyewear. The only exception is a medical condition that physically prevents the removal of the glasses, documented by a signed physician's statement submitted with the application. Contact lenses are not glasses and are permitted.

requirements/australia-visa-photo-requir.h1: Australia Visa Photo Requirements: a 2026 Complete Guide

sections.title: Australia Visa Photo Requirements: a 2026 Complete Guide
items: Australian visa photo requirements are among the strictest in the world, and a compliant photo is a mandatory part of the application package. The image must be 35–40 mm wide and 45–50 mm high, taken within the last six months against a plain, light grey background, and show the applicant’s head and shoulders with a neutral expression and mouth closed. For the passport itself, the Australian passport photo size page prepares the same dimensions from a phone picture.

To increase the chances of approval on the first submission, it is essential to follow the full 2026 Australian visa photo specifications described in this guide, which have been checked and confirmed by our internal compliance team.
Source: DFAT

sections.title: 11 Essential Australia Visa Photo Requirements: Checklist
items: Australia visa photo requirements are determined by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and are based on the biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). For a visa application to be accepted, the photos submitted with it must fully comply with the official guidelines listed below.
Parameter
Requirement
1. Number of photos
One digital photo is required when applying for your visa online via ImmiAccount . Two printed photos may be requested by the visa service provider for an in-person paper application.
2. Recency
A visa photo for Australia must be taken within the last six months of the application and exactly reflect the applicant's current appearance.
3. Australia visa photo size

Australia visa photo size is 35–40 mm wide and 45–50 mm high — the DFAT requires the same dimensions for visa pictures as for the passport photos. The head must take 70-80% of the image, or 32-36 mm from the chin to the top of the head. The passport rules differ in the background colour, and the PhotoGov Australian passport photo guide sets them out in full.
4. Colour
Only coloured photos are accepted for Australian visa applications. The colours in the picture must accurately show the applicant's natural skin tone and hair colour.
5. Background
A plain, light grey background , free of textures or patterns, is required for Australian visa photos.
6. Lighting
Even, uniform lighting with no harsh shadows or reflections.
7. Positioning and framing
Head in close-up, square to the camera , no tilting of head or shoulders.
8. Facial expression
Neutral expression, eyes open, mouth closed ; no smiling, frowning, or exaggerated expressions.
9. Clothing, headwear, and accessories

Normal clothes; avoid uniforms, camouflage, turtlenecks, or overly casual attire . Solid colors contrasting with the background are recommended. No hats or head coverings unless for religious or medical reasons, and they must not obscure facial features. Hearing aids are allowed.
10. Glasses
Generally discouraged . Allowed only for medical reasons with a supporting certificate, and lenses must be free of glare and reflections. Tinted glasses and sunglasses are not allowed.
11. Print and Digital quality

For in-person applications , visa photos must be professionally printed on photo paper. Digital visa photo must be 826 × 1062 pixels, JPEG, 70 KB-3.5 MB, free from pixelation, digital noise, and alterations, including red-eye removal.
You can use our online tool to make an Australian visa photo that meets all official requirements, including format, size, background, composition, and image quality.

A digital photo must fall into the 826 × 1062 pixels; the head takes 70-80% of the image requirements, with the file saved as a JPEG, sized 70 KB-3.5 MB.

Both printouts and digital photos must be recent, sharp, on a plain light grey background, with a neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open and clearly visible, and without digital retouching or filters.

sections.title: Where to Take an Australian Visa Photo?
items: You can get an Australian visa photo in many standard locations worldwide — from local photo labs and pharmacies to professional studios and online tools — as long as they can follow Australian size and biometric rules (typically 35–40 mm × 45–50 mm, face 32–36 mm from chin to crown, plain light grey background).

sections.title: Local Photo Labs and Retail Photo Counters
items: Most countries have chain photo labs, minilabs in supermarkets, or electronics and office retailers with photo counters that can print visa and passport photos to custom sizes. When using them for an Australian visa, you need to explicitly ask for Australian visa dimensions (usually 35–40 mm wide and 45–50 mm high, with a face 32–36 mm), a plain light grey background, and a recent, sharp colour print.

sections.title: Post Offices
items: Many postal operators (for example, USPS in the United States, Canada Post in Canada, Deutsche Post/DHL in Germany, La Poste in France, or Royal Mail in the United Kingdom) offer passport/visa photo services. These locations usually have calibrated setups for multiple countries’ visas and can produce an Australia visa photo size on request, with correct framing and a light grey background.

sections.title: Self-Service Photo Booths
items: Photo booths in shopping centres, metro stations, and high‑traffic areas often support several international formats, including the Australian visa photo size. However, for Australian visas, they are a risky option: images are frequently rejected for shadows, incorrect distance, wrong head size, or uneven lighting, so booths should be treated as a last resort if you do not have access to a studio or online service.

sections.title: Professional Studios and Dedicated ID‑Photo Providers
items: Professional photo studios and specialised ID‑photo providers are the most reliable offline option for Australian visa photos. They can set even lighting, provide a plain white or light grey background, and match Australian and ICAO standards for photo size and head proportions (35–40 × 45–50 mm, face 32–36 mm from chin to crown, head about 70–80% of the frame). Many studios will supply both printed photos and a compliant digital file for upload to ImmiAccount.

sections.title: Pharmacies and Convenience Chains
items: In many countries, large pharmacy and convenience chains operate small photo counters or kiosks for passport and visa photos. This is a convenient “on the way” option, but staff expertise and knowledge of Australian requirements vary by branch. It is important to confirm that they can produce an Australian visa photo in the correct dimensions with a plain light grey background, and to check whether a digital JPEG file for online submission is provided.

sections.title: Online Australian Passport Photo Makers
items: An online visa and passport photo maker is a reliable and convenient way to produce a compliant Australian visa photo.

You take a picture with a smartphone or camera, upload it to an Australian visa photo maker, and the system automatically crops it to the correct size 35-40 × 45-50 mm, scales the face to 32-36 mm (70-80% of the frame), corrects the background to a plain light grey colour, and saves the file in an appropriate JPEG size for upload to ImmiAccount or a printable PDF sheet.
After receiving your final photo, you can either submit the digital file directly with your online visa application or send it to any local photo lab for printing on photo paper.

sections.title: How to Take an Australian Visa Photo at Home
items: Taking an Australian visa photo in the correct 35–40×45–50 mm format at home is quick and straightforward when you use an online tool like PhotoGov. You can start with a simple smartphone portrait, and the platform automatically adjusts the background, proportions, and required settings. There’s no need for a photo studio visit — the finished result will meet all Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) visa and passport photo guidelines.

Set up your shot in a bright, evenly lit area — natural daylight beside a window is ideal. Make sure the background is perfectly plain white or light in color — cream, or pale gray. The light should evenly illuminate your face to avoid shadows or glare.

Hold your phone about 40–50 cm (16–20 in) away if using the front camera, or approximately 1 m (3 ft) away when using the back camera. Look directly at the lens, keep your head level, and maintain a calm, neutral expression. Take a few pictures to choose the sharpest one. Head coverings are only acceptable for religious or cultural reasons, and they must not obscure facial features.

Upload your chosen photo to PhotoGov and select “Australia” followed by your visa or document type. The automatic system will crop, resize, and align your image according to the latest visa photo rules.

If your submission is of high priority, consider adding the Human Verification — a senior expert with an embassy background will check your photo for Australian visa photo specifications compliance. If the photo needs corrections, you will be offered to retake it.
Once a 100% technically compliant image is produced, it can be lodged with your visa application, in person or online.

sections.title: Taking Australian Visa Photos of Children With an iPhone
items: Just as pictures of adult applicants, baby visa photos must also comply with the Department of Home Affairs requirements. Taking them at home is often simpler and more comfortable for both parent and child. With proper lighting and setting, your iPhone can easily capture a clear baby portrait that meets official standards.

Note that DFAT allows infants' mouths to be slightly open in visa photos. Once you've completed the mission, upload the image to an online Australian visa photo checker, and the system will instantly check and convert it into a compliant Australian visa photo.
Setting
Uniform lighting from a natural source, plain background.
Position
A newborn may lie on a blanket; older children — sit or stand.
Expression
Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing.
Frame
No toys, parents’ hands, or other objects in the frame.

sections.title: 10 Common Reasons for Australian Visa Photo Rejection
items: Australian visa photo submissions are frequently refused due to technical non-compliance or poor image quality. The most typical problems include:

Non-compliant dimensions : The photo does not fall within the required 35–40 mm width and 45–50 mm height, or the face is too large or too small relative to the frame (must be 32–36 mm from chin to crown).
Improper background : Background is not plain and light (white or light grey), or shows gradients, shadows, or visible texture.
Inconsistent lighting : Uneven illumination, harsh shadows, or bright spots that distort facial features.
Non-neutral pose : Head turned, tilted, or facial expression not neutral (e.g., smiling or raised eyebrows).
Poor technical quality : Lack of sharpness, visible compression artifacts, or insufficient resolution.
Face partially obscured : Hair, accessories, or objects covering key facial areas such as eyes or jawline.
Unacceptable accessories : Glasses, tinted lenses, or headwear that is not for religious or medical purposes.
Outdated photo : The image does not reflect your current look due to a time gap or noticeable changes.
AI manipulations : Use of filters, AI enhancement, or retouching that alters skin tone, texture, or facial structure
Printing defects (if applicable): Low-quality output, incorrect colors, or physical damage to the photo.
Online visa photo tools help minimize these risks by automatically aligning the image with Australian requirements, including correct sizing, background normalization, and facial positioning.

sections.title: What to Do if Your Australian Visa Photo Is Rejected
items: If your photo is not accepted, the immigration system will indicate the reason for rejection.
For digital submissions: Replace the image directly in ImmiAccount with a corrected version that meets all specifications.
For paper-based applications: Provide new printed photos that fully comply with the requirements.
Resubmitting a photo does not incur additional charges unless your visa application has lapsed.

If you used an online photo service to create your Australian visa picture, you can typically request a correction or refund, provided the issue relates to technical compliance rather than the original image quality.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What are the Key Australian Visa Photo Requirements?
items: Here is a list of essential Australian visa photo specifications. Follow them to avoid visa delays or rejections:
Size: 35–40 mm wide and 45–50 mm high, head 32–36 mm from chin to crown.
Framing : Face centred, head straight, filling about 70–80% of the photo.
Background : Plain white or light-coloured, evenly lit, with no patterns or shadows.
Quality: Recent colour photo (within 6 months), sharp, in focus, no filters or retouching.
Appearance: Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, no glasses or non‑religious headwear blocking the face.

sections.title: How Recent Should My Photo Be for an Australian Visa?
items: Your picture must be taken within the past six months and clearly reflect your current appearance.

sections.title: Can I apply for an Australian Visa Using Digital Photos?
items: Yes. If you're applying online via the ImmiAccount , you must submit a digital photo with your application.

sections.title: Can I Use my Australia Visa Photo for Another Application?
items: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) sets the same requirements for visa and passport photos. You can use your passport photo to apply for an Australian visa, and vice versa.

sections.title: What is the Australian Visa Photo Size?
items: 35–40 × 45–50 mm is the official passport photo size range set by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia for passport-sized photos. This is why the 35×45 mm format is widely used for Australian visa photos, as it sits comfortably within these standard measurements and is accepted for most applications.​

sections.title: What is Australia Student Visa Photo Size?
items: For an Australian student visa, the required photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with your head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown and centred against a plain light background. This format matches the standard Australian visa photo dimensions used across visitor, student, and work visa subclasses.

sections.title: What is Australia Visitor Visa Photo Size?
items: For an Australian visitor visa, the standard photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown and centered against a plain light or light grey background.

sections.title: What is Australia Visa Photo Size in CM?
items: Australia visa photos must be between 3.5–4.0 cm wide and 4.5–5.0 cm high, with the face taking roughly 70–80% of the image (about 3.2–3.6 cm from chin to crown). Any size within this 3.5–4.0 × 4.5–5.0 cm range is acceptable.

sections.title: What is Australia Visa Photo Size in Inches?
items: Australia visa photo size in inches is 1.38–1.57 inches wide and 1.77–1.97 inches high.

sections.title: Can Head Coverings be Used in Australian Visa Pictures?
items: No. The only two exceptions — if they are religious head coverings worn daily for religious reasons; another acceptable reason is medical, for example, if the head covering is necessary after a surgery. In this case, an applicant must provide a signed certificate from their medical provider.

sections.title: Can I Wear Makeup in my Australian Visa Picture?
items: Yes, you can, but only if it doesn't obstruct or alter your facial features in any way. Reflective makeup that can cause glare or reflections should be avoided.

sections.title: How to Print my Australian Visa Picture?
items: Make sure your visa photos are printed on premium matte or glossy paper for physical submissions. Check that your digital file satisfies the necessary resolution and file size before uploading your online entry — preferably, 600 DPI, and the size falls into a 35–40 × 45–50 mm range, with the head taking 70-80% of the image.

sections.title: How to Make a Perfect Australian Visa Picture With an iPhone?
items: Follow these 7 steps to make a perfect visa picture with your iPhone, and our tool will handle all the necessary adjustments to provide you with a 100% photo.
Lighting: Use even, soft light to avoid shadows.
iPhone: Keep it steady at eye level, turn off Portrait mode.
Background: Must be plain. Stand against a plain, light-colored wall.
Posture: Face the camera straight with relaxed, straight shoulders.
Capture. Capture a few shots and choose the best one.
Process. Upload your selfie to a reliable online photo-making tool to convert it into an official visa picture.
Download. Get a ready photo in digital format or a PDF printable sheet.

sections.title: What are the Typical Issues in Visa Photos and How to Avoid Them?
items: Here is a short list of typical issues with visa pictures:
Glare on glasses: Remove glasses or adjust the light so there are no reflections.
Uneven background: Use our background removal tool for a smooth, uniform backdrop.
Incorrect sizing: Double-check the dimensions, and correct the crop with our tool.
Shadows: Avoid any shadows on your face when taking a visa photo.

sections.title: Do Children Need a Different Australian Visa Photo?
items: No. Australian visa photos of children must meet the same technical standards as adults: 35–40 × 45–50 mm photo size, 32–36 mm head height, plain light grey background, and a neutral expression. For infants, the child must be alone in the frame, lying on a light blanket or seated in a chair, with no visible hands, toys, or support, eyes open where possible, and no hats or headbands covering the forehead or ears.

sections.title: Can I Take an Australian Visa Photo at Home?
items: Yes. You can take it at home if you reproduce studio-like conditions: place the camera or phone at eye level about 1.5–2 m away, stand in front of a flat light-coloured wall, and use soft, even light (for example, facing a window) so there are no shadows on your face or background. Take several shots with a neutral expression and then use a visa photo tool such as PhotoGov to crop the image to 35–40 × 45–50 mm and adjust the head to 32–36 mm from chin to crown.

sections.title: Can I Use a Selfie for an Australian Visa Photo?
items: Yes, but only if it’s taken correctly. The best way is to use a tripod or stand, set the camera at eye level directly in front of you, use a timer or remote, and produce a straight, undistorted portrait that meets all size and background rules.

sections.title: Are Glasses Allowed in Australian Visa Photos?
items: You should remove glasses whenever possible, as reflections, frame shadows, and covered pupils are common rejection reasons. If you cannot remove them for medical reasons, only clear, untinted lenses without glare and thin frames that do not cut across the eyes or eyebrows are acceptable; sunglasses and photochromic (darkening) lenses are not allowed.

sections.title: Do I Need to Remove Facial Piercings for My Visa Photo?
items: There is no blanket ban on facial piercings, but the photo will be rejected if jewellery hides facial contours, casts visible shadows, or produces strong reflections. Small, matte studs usually cause no issues, while large rings, tunnels, or shiny metal pieces should be removed for the photo to minimise the risk of refusal.

sections.title: Can I Smile in My Australian Visa Photo?
items: No. Even a slight smile is considered non-compliant if it changes the shape of your mouth or cheeks or shows teeth. You must keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed, eyes open, and facial muscles relaxed so that biometric measurements remain accurate.

sections.title: What are Australia Visa Photo Dimensions for Digital Uploads?
items: For an online Australian visa application, you must upload 1 digital photo through

ImmiAccount . The image must be 826 × 1062 pixels, saved in JPEG format, and the file size must be between 70 KB and 3.5 MB. Your head should occupy about 70–80% of the image, which corresponds to the standard Australian visa photo proportions.

sections.title: How Many Australian Visa Photos Do I Need to Submit?
items: For online applications, you normally upload one digital photo per applicant through ImmiAccount. For paper-based applications, most forms require two identical printed photos, but you must follow the exact number stated in the instructions for that particular visa form.

sections.title: Can I Use a Black-and-White Photo for an Australian Visa?
items: No. Australian visa photos must be in colour to show natural skin tones and clear detail; black-and-white or monochrome images are not accepted.

sections.title: Is a Beard or New Hairstyle a Problem for My Visa Photo?
items: A beard, moustache, or new hairstyle is not a problem as long as your photo is less than 6 months old and your face is fully visible. Issues arise only when facial hair or haircuts obscure the jawline, cheeks, eyes, or eyebrows, in which case you should adjust your hair or trim your beard and retake the photo.

sections.title: Can I Edit the Background of My Australian Visa Photo?
items: Yes. You may clean and standardise the background to a plain light grey colour using online tools like an Australia visa photo checker or an Australia visa photo editor, provided the outline of your head and face is not altered, and no visible artefacts appear around the hair. Any editing that smooths skin, reshapes features, or otherwise changes your natural appearance is not acceptable.

sections.title: What Should My Child Wear for an Australian Visa Photo?
items: Dress your child in everyday clothes that contrast with the light grey background, such as mid-tone or darker tops without large logos or bright patterns. Avoid white shirts that blend into the background, anything resembling a uniform, and any hoods, hats, or headbands that cover the forehead, ears, or hairline.

sections.title: Are Earphones or Headphones Allowed in Australian Visa Photos?
items: No. All earphones, earbuds, headphones, and headsets must be removed before the photo is taken; no electronic devices or accessories should appear in the picture.
PhotoGov.net strictly adheres to the Global regulations for ID photos .

requirements/bangladesh-passport-photo.h1: Bangladesh Passport Photo Requirements: All You Need to Know in 2026

sections.title: Bangladesh Passport Photo Requirements: All You Need to Know in 2026
items: In most cases, you don’t need to provide a photo for your Bangladesh passport in 2026: the enrolment officer captures the biometric photo live at the passport office or a mission abroad. A printed photo is used only in two cases: 3R-print files for children under six, and an older Machine Readable Passport (MRP) reissue that requires 45 × 55 mm printed photos. Always double-check the instructions if you’re applying from the Bangladesh mission abroad — the specs may differ. This guide covers all official Bangladesh photo rules in 2026 so you submit the correct photo, or get ready for an in-office capture, avoiding delays or rejections.

sections.title: 12 Key Bangladesh Passport Photo Requirements: a Checklist
items: The Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) and the Bangladesh e-Passport Portal set the national specifications for passport photos. These rules are based on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 biometric photo standards.

Bangladesh began issuing e-Passports on 22 January 2020, becoming the first South Asian country to roll them out nationwide. Today, the e-Passport is Bangladesh’s standard format for new applications and renewals. Limited MRP reissue services may still be available in specific cases. An e-Passport carries an embedded chip that stores the holder's photo, fingerprints, and iris scan, all captured during a biometric enrolment appointment.

The older Machine Readable Passport (MRP) is being phased out and can no longer be requested as a fresh application . An older MRP has no chip. It relies on a printed, machine-readable data page. Bangladesh no longer issues new MRPs, and this format now applies to a narrow group only — applicants completing an MRP reissue on a passport they already hold. In these cases, a photo still has to be submitted with the paper application but not captured live, because there's no biometric enrolment step to capture it.

The same applies to children under six — a child that age can't reliably complete biometric enrolment , so this application uses a printed 3R photo instead of live capture — even though the document being issued is still an e-Passport.
Below are the 12 official requirements that every photo submitted with a passport application must meet exactly, no matter the submission method.
Requirement
Details
1. Number of Photos
One photo is required per applicant. Add one photo of each parent when the applicant is 15 or younger.
2. Recency
The photo must be taken specifically for this application . An old passport or ID photo is not accepted.
3. Photo Size
Live capture is sized and framed automatically by the enrolment system. A 3R print for children under 6 measures 3.5 × 5 in (9 × 13 cm). An MRP-printed photo must be 55 × 45 mm.
4. Colour
The photo must be in full colour , with accurate skin tone and clear facial detail.
5. Background
A plain grey background is officially required for e-Passports. A Bangladesh mission abroad may require a different colour; always double-check it.
6. Lighting
Lighting must be even and free of shadows. The eyes, nose, mouth, chin, and full facial outline must stay clearly visible.
7. Positioning and Framing
The camera must face the applicant directly. The head must be upright and centred, with both sides of the face visible and clear space around the head.
8. Facial Expression
A neutral expression is required: mouth closed, both eyes open, gaze on the camera. Smiling, frowning, and raised eyebrows are not permitted.
9. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories
Clothing must contrast with the background. Hair and any head covering must leave the forehead, cheeks, chin, eyes, and facial outline visible. Full requirements below.
10. Glasses
Glasses come off for live capture if the officer asks. In a printed photo, both eyes must be fully visible, free of glare and frame obstruction. Full requirements below.
11. Digital Quality
Live capture is stored automatically by the enrolment system. A digital MRP photo must be a genuine, unaltered image, sized for the lab to print at 45 × 55 mm.
12. Print Quality
Every printed photo must come from a professional photo lab. It must be sharp and evenly coloured, with no creases or damaged edges.

sections.title: Clothing, Head Coverings, and Glasses in Bangladesh Passport Photos
What Clothes Should I Wear in a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Your clothing needs to contrast with the photo's grey background, so the outline of your shoulders and collar stays distinct from the backdrop behind you. White, cream, and other pale tones blend into the background and are one of the most common reasons a printed photo is rejected. Uniforms, camouflage patterns, and any clothing that resembles official government or military dress are not accepted, regardless of the applicant's profession. Beyond colour, the requirement is straightforward: everyday clothing, worn as you normally would, is what the passport office expects to see.

sections.title: Are Head Coverings Allowed in a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Religious and medical head coverings are both fully permitted, and an applicant is never asked to remove one for a Bangladesh passport photo. The requirement that applies to every head covering, whatever the reason it is worn, is visibility: the face must remain completely visible from the hairline to the bottom of the chin, with no shadow or fabric crossing the forehead, cheeks, or chin.

For a hijab, veil, turban, or patka worn daily for religious reasons, the fabric should frame the face rather than cross into it — the edge should sit at the hairline, not lower. The same standard applies to a medical head covering, such as a surgical cap, a bandage, or a wig or scarf worn after hair loss from treatment: the face still needs to be fully visible, because a medical reason does not relax the biometric standard.

What is not accepted is a head covering worn for style rather than a religious or medical reason — a hat, cap, headband, or fashion scarf, for example. And regardless of why it is worn, any covering that casts a shadow across the face or covers the forehead, cheeks, chin, eyes, or jawline will cause the photo to be rejected.

sections.title: Can I Wear Glasses in a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Glasses are allowed in a Bangladesh passport photo, provided both eyes remain completely visible: no glare across either lens, and no part of the frame covering the eyes. This applies regardless of why the applicant wears them. What is not accepted is glare or reflection on the lenses, a frame thick enough to cross the eye or pupil, tinted or photochromic lenses that darken the eyes, and sunglasses of any kind — all of these cause rejection, prescription or not.
For live capture, the enrolment officer makes this call in the moment. If the applicant is asked to remove their glasses, they will need to do so before the image is captured.

sections.title: Acceptable Bangladesh Passport Photo Examples Unacceptable Bangladesh Passport Photo Examples
What Type of Photo Do I Need for My Bangladesh Passport?
items: The type of photo (printed or captured at the moment of physical passport application) depends on your application type:
Application Type
Photo Required
Standard e-Passport application, age six and above (first-time or renewal)
Live capture at the enrolment appointment. No photo is prepared or brought in advance.
Passport application for a child under six
A printed 3R photo, 3.5 × 5 in (9 × 13 cm), prepared before the appointment and brought to enrolment for scanning.
MRP reissue (existing MRP holders only — Bangladesh no longer issues new MRPs)
A printed 55 × 45 mm photo, with 30 × 25 mm spaces for each parent's photo when the applicant is 15 or younger.
Application through a Bangladesh mission abroad
Live capture at the mission, following the same rule as a domestic application. Where a 3R print is required instead, the mission's own published checklist sets the background and size to follow.

sections.title: Photo Captured Live During the Appointment
items: Live capture happens at the enrolment appointment: the officer photographs the applicant on the spot, using the equipment installed at that office or mission, with no printed photo needed. However, if your application requires a printed photo — it is your responsibility to have the photo taken and printed in advance.

sections.title: Regional and Divisional Passport Offices
items: Applicants in Bangladesh go to the regional or divisional passport office assigned through their e-Passport application. Wear clothing that contrasts with the background before arriving, and once seated, follow the officer's instructions on posture and where to look — live capture happens right there, during the appointment.

sections.title: Missions Abroad
items: Applicants outside Bangladesh go to the Bangladesh mission listed in their application instead of a domestic passport office. Before arranging a 3R print, check that mission's own published checklist: the background colour is set centrally, but individual missions may specify a different one, and shooting to the wrong colour means a reprint.

sections.title: RPO Bangladesh Secretariat and Dhaka Cantonment
items: Applicants using the dedicated Bangladesh Secretariat or Dhaka Cantonment form go through the identical live-capture process as everyone else, once the responsible office has confirmed their eligibility for that specific appointment.

sections.title: Preparing a Printed Photo for Children Under Six or MRP Applications
items: Only two cases require preparing a photo in advance: a child under six, or an MRP application. Every other applicant simply attends their enrolment appointment for live capture.
Confirm the background required. Grey under the central rule, the specific colour required by the mission for applicants abroad, or whatever the MRP form specifies.
Light the shot evenly and position the camera at eye level , facing the subject directly. For a child, have another adult hold the camera and keep the child alone in frame.
Keep the head upright and centred , with hair and any head covering clear of the forehead, cheeks, chin, and eyes.
Choose clothing that contrasts with the background. Avoid large prints, grey, white, bright colours, large logos, camouflage, and military-looking wear.

Take several photographs and select the sharpest, most evenly lit one. Beauty filters and edits that alter facial features are not permitted. Basic cropping, resizing, and background preparation are acceptable when the final image remains natural and meets the required specifications.
Order the correct print : a 3R print (3.5 × 5 in) or an MRP print (55 × 45 mm), depending on the application.

sections.title: Getting a Printed Bangladesh Passport Photo at a Photo Studio
items: If you are required to bring in a printed photo, a professional photo studio is a reliable choice. The staff is familiar with Bangladesh passport photo requirements and will professionally print out the ready shot in a required format — either at 3R or 55 × 45 mm. It's worth checking the print before submitting it: the dimensions should be exact, the colour accurate, the detail sharp, and the surface free of creases or damage.

sections.title: Getting a Printable MRP Photo Online
items: For applicants who prefer not to spend time and money on a studio visit, PhotoGov's Bangladesh passport photo maker is a reliable choice. All you need is a good-quality input selfie taken in sufficient daylight. The online tool automatically resizes, frames, and crops it to a 55 × 45 mm file that you download as a professional-grade printable PDF file. This option saves you time and money, providing the output tailored to the exact Bangladesh passport photo standards.

sections.title: 10 Common Reasons for Bangladesh Passport Photo Rejection
items: Wrong photo type submitted. A studio print is provided when live capture applies; it must come from the enrolment officer instead.
Incorrect print size. A 3R print that isn't exactly 3.5 × 5 in (9 × 13 cm) is rejected.
Wrong background colour. Grey is required, unless the mission abroad specifies otherwise.
Dark or blurred image. Uneven lighting or soft focus causes rejection.
Tilted or turned head. The camera must face the applicant directly, with eyes level and the head upright.
Unsuitable expression. Anything other than a calm face, closed mouth, open eyes, and a direct gaze is rejected.
Glasses obscuring the eyes. Glare, tinted lenses, or a frame crossing the eyes causes rejection.
Face partially covered. Hair or a head covering crossing the forehead, cheeks, chin, eyes, or jawline is rejected.
Filters or retouching applied. The photo must be a genuine, unaltered capture.
Print sizes confused. 3R and MRP serve different forms; ordering the wrong one means a reshoot.

sections.title: What to Do if a Bangladesh Passport Photo Is Rejected
items: The enrolment officer explains exactly what needs to change, and the fix depends on which type of photo failed. For live capture, the applicant follows the officer's correction — posture, clothing, glasses, hair, or expression — and a new photo is taken on the spot. For a printed photo, the applicant confirms the size and background with the officer, then orders a fresh print from a professional lab. A blurred, unevenly lit, poorly framed, or retouched image always needs a new photograph; the rejected file cannot be corrected after the fact. If PhotoGov prepared the MRP file, send the officer's exact correction to PhotoGov support before ordering another print.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What is the Bangladesh Passport Photo Size and Format?
items: Live capture is sized and formatted automatically at enrolment. A child under six needs a 3R colour print measuring 3.5 × 5 in, roughly 9 × 13 cm. An MRP application uses a 55 × 45 mm photo where the issued form requires it, with 30 × 25 mm spaces for the parents' photos when the applicant is under 15.

sections.title: What are the Essential Bangladesh Passport Photo Requirements?
items: Four things determine acceptance for a printed photo: a grey background (or the colour set by the mission abroad), even lighting with the full facial outline visible, an upright head with a neutral expression, and clothing that contrasts with the background. Live capture applies the identical standard automatically.

sections.title: Where to Take a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Live capture takes place at the regional or divisional passport office inside Bangladesh, or at the Bangladesh mission abroad. A studio or photo lab is only involved for the printed-photo cases.

sections.title: How to Prepare for Live Bangladesh e-Passport Capture?
items: Wear clothing that contrasts with the background, and keep the forehead, cheeks, chin, eyes, and facial outline visible. Glasses come off if the officer asks. Head upright, gaze directed at the lens, expression neutral.

sections.title: What are the Bangladesh Passport Photo Rules for Children Under Six?
items: A studio or photo lab produces the 3R print, matching the background specified by the processing office or mission. Another adult holds the camera at the child's eye level, keeps the child alone in frame under even lighting, and sends the sharpest frame to the lab for printing.

sections.title: How Many Photos are Required for My Bangladesh Passport Application?
items: Live capture covers most applicants. A printed photo needs one copy — 3R or MRP — plus one photo of each parent when the applicant is 15 or younger.

sections.title: How Much is the Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Live capture is included in the application fee. Printed-photo cases run on the rate charged by the studio, lab, or online tool used to produce them.

sections.title: Can You Wear Glasses in a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Yes, provided both eyes are fully visible, free of glare, and unobstructed by the frame. Glasses come off for live capture if the officer asks, and sunglasses or tinted lenses are never accepted.

sections.title: Are Religious Head Coverings Allowed in Bangladesh Passport Photos?
items: Yes. A hijab, veil, turban, or patka worn daily for religious reasons is permitted, provided the face stays fully visible from hairline to chin.

sections.title: Are Medical Head Coverings Allowed in Bangladesh Passport Photos?
items: Yes, under the same standard as a religious head covering. A surgical cap, bandage, or covering worn for hair loss or a scalp condition is accepted as long as the face remains fully visible.

sections.title: Can You Smile in a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: No. A neutral expression is required — mouth closed, both eyes open, gaze on the camera. Smiling, frowning, and a tilted head all cause rejection.

sections.title: What Background Is Required for a Bangladesh Passport Photo?
items: Plain grey, under the central e-Passport rule. A Bangladesh mission abroad may require a different colour, so its published checklist should be checked before arranging a printed photo.

sections.title: What Happens if a Bangladesh Passport Photo is Rejected?
items: The enrolment officer explains exactly what needs to change. For live capture, a new photo is taken on the spot. For a printed photo, a new print is ordered from a professional lab once the correction is confirmed.

sections.title: Can You Use an Old Passport Photo for a New Application?
items: No. Every photo must be taken specifically for the current application — a photo from a previous passport, visa, or ID is not accepted.

sections.title: Where to Find the Official Bangladesh Passport Photo Rules?
items: The Bangladesh e-Passport Portal's Photo FAQ publishes the official rules. Applicants abroad should also check the passport page published by their specific Bangladesh mission.

requirements/german-passport.h1: German Passport Photo Requirements in 2026 — Learn New All-Digital Rules

sections.title: German Passport Photo Requirements in 2026 — Learn New All-Digital Rules
items: Planning to submit a photo and need to know the current German passport photo requirements? Since 1 May 2025, German passport photos (Biometrisches Passbild) are submitted only in electronic format — there is no printed photo to hand in at the counter.

Your German passport photo must be a colour image in the 35 × 45 mm format (413 × 531 pixels), with a plain light-grey background, and the face taking 70–80% of the frame. The photo is submitted online to your local citizens’ office ( Bürgeramt / Passbehörde ) with a QR code from a certified photographer or a Bürgeramt self-service terminal.
In this guide, we cover everything you need to know about German passport photos in 2026 — each requirement has been checked and verified by our compliance team against official sources.

sections.title: 12 Key German Passport Photo Requirements: a Checklist
items: German biometric photo requirements are set by the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) and Bundesdruckerei and align with the international biometric standard International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303. The table below consolidates all official specifications — covering size, background, colour, recency, and the digital submission channel.
Parameter
Requirement
1. Number of photos
One digital biometric photo. There is no printed copy to hand over — the image is captured and transmitted electronically.
2. Recency
Taken within the last 6 months, reflecting your current appearance. A new photo is required after any significant change in looks.
3. Size and head position
35 × 45 mm format (413 × 531 pixels). The face must fill 70–80% of the height — 32–36 mm from chin to crown (tolerance 27–40 mm) — centred and upright, neither tilted nor turned.
4. Background
Plain, light/neutral grey — not white. Medium grey for light or blonde hair, light grey for dark hair. No patterns, shadows, objects, or other people in the frame.
5. Lighting
Even lighting with natural skin tones. No shadows or reflections on the face or background, and no red-eye.
6. Facial expression and positioning
Look straight at the camera with a neutral expression, eyes open and clearly visible, mouth closed.
7. Clothing
Everyday clothing in colours that contrast with the grey background. No uniforms. Daily religious clothing is allowed if the full face stays visible.
8. Head coverings
Not permitted, except when worn daily for religious reasons, in which case the full face from chin to forehead must be visible, with no shadows.
9. Eyeglasses
Allowed only if the eyes are fully visible — no glare or reflection, no tinted lenses or sunglasses, and frames must not cover any part of the eyes. If unsure, remove them.
10. Appearance change
The photo must match your current appearance. After facial surgery or another significant change in looks, submit a new photo.
11. Submission format
Digital only — via a QR code or a biometric terminal. Since 1 May 2025 the image is sent through the encrypted government system; photos handed over on paper are rejected.
12. File and image quality
A colour JPEG, 413 × 531 pixels, sharp and high-contrast. Clean and undamaged, with no pixelation, filters, or AI editing. The certified system handles the file encoding automatically.

Use PhotoGov’s German Passport Photo Maker to turn a selfie into a compliance-aligned photo in under a minute — formatted to the official 35 × 45 mm (413 × 531 px) size, grey background, and face-coverage rules.

sections.title: Acceptable German Passport Photos
Unacceptable German Passport Photos
Germany’s Digital-Only Passport Photo Rule: What Changed in 2025
items: Germany implemented the most significant passport photo reform in its history on 1 May 2025 . From that date, all applications for passports, national ID cards, and residence permits must include a digitally submitted biometric photo.

Printed photos handed over at the counter are no longer accepted under any circumstances. This makes Germany one of the first countries in the world to fully eliminate printed passport photo submissions .

sections.title: How to Submit a Digital Photo for a German Passport
items: There are two approved routes for submitting a digital biometric photo in Germany:

Self-service biometric terminals (Selbstbedienungsterminals) are installed at Bürgerämter in most major cities. The applicant photographs themselves directly at the terminal; the system checks compliance and uploads the image automatically.

Certified photographers who have registered with the official e-passport photo system. The photographer captures the photo, encrypts and uploads it to the secure government platform (a cloud procedure certified by the Federal Office for Information Security, BSI), and gives the applicant a QR code (data-matrix code). The applicant presents this QR code at the Bürgeramt when submitting their application.

The encrypted photo transfer system is designed to prevent photo manipulation — specifically morphing attacks in which multiple faces are digitally blended to create fraudulent identity documents. The legal framework is the Act to Strengthen Security in Passport, ID and Foreigner Documentation (Gesetz zur Stärkung der Sicherheit im Pass-, Ausweis- und Ausländerdokumentenwesen), passed in 2020 and implemented in stages.
Germany Digital Passport Photos: Key Dates
1 May 2025 — Digital-only requirement came into force
31 July 2025 — Three-month transition period ended; printed photos rejected under all circumstances from this date
If you had passport photos professionally printed before May 2025 and have not yet used them, they cannot be accepted for a German identity document application.

sections.title: German Passport Photo Background: Grey, Not White
items: Germany’s background requirement is one of the most commonly misunderstood specifications in German passport photography. It fundamentally differs from many other countries, which require a pure white background.

The official Bundesdruckerei specification requires a plain, uniform, neutral grey background . The official sample photo guidance explicitly states that the background must be in a contrasting colour to the face and hair:
For applicants with light or blonde hair : a medium-grey background is specified, to provide sufficient contrast.
For applicants with dark hair : a light-grey background is specified.

A pure white background is not accepted as it may actually reduce contrast for light-haired applicants. A patterned background, shadows on the background, a second person, or an object visible in the frame are all grounds for rejection. The background must be of solid colour throughout with no gradients, textures, or shadows.

sections.title: Glasses in German Passport Photos
items: Unlike India (which introduced an absolute glasses ban in September 2025) or the United States (which banned glasses in 2016), Germany’s official specification permits glasses under specific conditions. The eyes must be clearly visible in the photograph. This means:
No flash reflection or glare on the lenses
No tinted lenses or sunglasses of any kind
The edge of the lenses or frames must not cover any part of the eyes

In practice, compliance with all three conditions simultaneously can be difficult to achieve, especially with modern anti-reflective coatings. Certified photographers are trained to manage lighting to avoid reflection. If any of the three conditions cannot be met, removing glasses before the photo is taken is the simplest solution and guarantees compliance.

You can photograph yourself at a Bürgeramt terminal, visit a certified photographer or drugstore that uploads the image for you, or prepare a fully compliant image online with PhotoGov before your appointment. sections.title: German Passport Photos for Minors: BMI Guidelines by Age
Children Aged 10 to 17: Full Adult Specifications Apply
items: From age 10, all standard specifications apply without modification. The child must face the camera directly, maintain a neutral expression with the mouth closed, and keep the eyes fully open. The face must take up 70–80% of the photo (face height 32–36 mm). No glasses are recommended to avoid compliance risk. Religious head coverings follow the same rules as for adults.

sections.title: Children Aged 6 to 9
items: The face may take up 50–80% of the photo, with the head height (chin to crown) between 22 and 36 mm; photos are rejected only below 17 mm or above 40 mm. A neutral expression, direct gaze at the camera, and a centred head are still required at this age.

sections.title: Children Aged 5 and Under
items: The same facial-size measurements apply (face 50–80%, height 22–36 mm). Children in this age group do not need to maintain a neutral expression, look directly at the camera, or have their heads centred in the frame.

sections.title: Babies Under 1 Year
items: All the same specifications as for children aged 5 and under apply. Additionally, babies under one year do not need to have their eyes open. Photos of babies may be taken lying on a plain grey or white sheet with the camera directly overhead, or held upright with both supporting hands completely out of the frame. No toys, dummies, or other objects may be visible.

sections.title: Common Reasons for a German Passport Photo Rejection
items: 1. Submission of a printed photo. Since 31 July 2025, paper photos are no longer accepted. A QR code from a certified photographer or a terminal-captured image is required.
2. Incorrect or low-contrast background. A white or cream background may fail the contrast check, particularly for light-haired applicants. Use a proper neutral grey backdrop.
3. Shadows on the background. The applicant must stand far enough from the backdrop that their body casts no shadow onto it.
4. Glare or reflection on eyeglasses. The most common glasses-related rejection. Lighting must be even and positioned to eliminate lens glare entirely.
5. Insufficient face height. A face below the 32 mm optimum (or below 22 mm for children aged 9 and under; hard rejection below 27 mm, or below 17 mm for young children). Move closer to the camera.
6. Excessive face height. A face above 36 mm (or above 40 mm, the absolute tolerance limit). Increase the distance between the applicant and the camera.
7. Incorrect head position. The face must be photographed en face — both ears at the same height, looking straight into the lens, neither tilted nor turned.
8. Non-neutral facial expression. An open mouth or even a slight smile changes facial geometry and can fail automated biometric checks.
9. Uneven facial lighting and shadows. Uneven lighting creates shadows across the nose, chin, or forehead. Two light sources positioned symmetrically on either side of the camera prevent this.
10. Insufficient image quality or resolution. Blurred or pixelated images are explicitly rejected. Submit a sharp, high-quality 413 × 531-pixel image.

sections.title: What to Do If Your German Passport Photo Is Rejected
items: A rejection is rarely the end of the process. Because the compliance check happens before your document is produced — at the terminal, in the photographer’s software, or at the counter — you can correct the issue quickly. Follow these steps.

1. Identify the exact reason. A biometric self-service terminal or a certified photographer’s software flags the specific fault (background, head size, glare, expression, sharpness). If the photo is rejected at the counter, the official will tell you which rule was not met.

2. Retake the photo — do not edit it. German biometric photos must be genuine and unaltered, and retouched or AI-edited images are detectable and rejected. Capture a new photo that corrects the flagged issue rather than trying to “fix” the old one.

3. Re-capture through an approved channel. Photograph yourself again at the Bürgeramt terminal, or ask your certified photographer to re-shoot and re-upload the image; they will issue a new QR code at no extra charge in most studios.

4. Pre-check before you submit. To avoid a repeat rejection, run your image through an automated compliance check — such as PhotoGov’s German passport photo maker — which verifies size, background, head position, and lighting before your appointment.
