sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What Are the Official German Passport Photo Requirements?
items: A German biometric passport photo (Biometrisches Passbild) must use the 35 × 45 mm format (413 × 531 pixels), with the face occupying 70–80% of the photo (height 32–36 mm from chin to crown). The background must be plain and bright — ideally neutral grey, contrasting with the applicant’s hair colour. The photo must be taken en face with a neutral expression, mouth closed, and eyes fully open. Since 1 May 2025, photos must be submitted digitally as a colour image via a QR code from a certified photographer or a biometric self-service terminal. Paper photos are no longer accepted.

sections.title: What Is the German Passport Photo Size in Pixels?
items: The German passport photo is 413 × 531 pixels. This is the standard digital size of the 35 × 45 mm format at 300 dpi, the resolution used for German ID photographs. The official BMI Fotomustertafel and the Federal Foreign Office sample sheet define the photo in millimetres (35 × 45 mm) and require a sharp, high-quality image with no pixelation; 413 × 531 px is the corresponding digital pixel size. Submit the image as a colour JPEG.

sections.title: Can I Still Hand In a Printed Photo at the Bürgeramt?
items: No. Germany ended paper passport photo submissions on 1 May 2025, with strict enforcement from 31 July 2025. All photo submissions must now be digital. You either photograph yourself at a biometric self-service terminal at the Bürgeramt or visit a certified photographer who uploads the image to the government system and provides you with a QR code.

sections.title: Does Germany Require a White or a Grey Background for Passport Photos?
items: Germany requires a grey background, not a white one — one of the biggest differences from countries such as the United States or India. The official Bundesdruckerei and Federal Foreign Office specifications call for a plain, uniform, bright background in a colour that contrasts with the applicant’s face and hair: a medium-grey background is specified for light or blonde hair, and a light-grey background for dark hair. A pure white background is not prescribed and can actually fail the contrast check for fair-haired applicants. The background must be a single colour throughout, with no patterns, gradients, shadows, or other people or objects in the frame.

sections.title: Are Glasses Allowed in German Passport Photos?
items: Yes, but only if all conditions are met: the eyes must be fully and clearly visible, there must be no flash reflection or glare on the lenses, no tinted lenses or sunglasses are worn, and the frames must not cover any part of the eyes. In practice, if any condition cannot be guaranteed, removing glasses before the photo is the safest approach.

sections.title: How Large Must the Face Be in a German Passport Photo?
items: The face — measured from the bottom of the chin to the crown of the head (not the top of the hair) — must be between 32 and 36 mm within the 35 × 45 mm format. This represents 70–80% of the photo height. Photos are only rejected at the hard tolerance limits of below 27 mm or above 40 mm, but the optimum range of 32–36 mm should always be targeted.

sections.title: What Are the Rules for Children’s German Passport Photos?
items: For children aged 10 and above, adult specifications apply in full (face 70–80%, height 32–36 mm, neutral expression, direct gaze). For children aged 9 and under, the face may occupy 50–80% of the photo, with a face-height range of 22–36 mm (rejected below 17 mm or above 40 mm). For children aged 5 and under, a neutral expression, direct gaze, and centred head are not required. Babies under 1 year do not need to have their eyes open.

sections.title: How Recent Must a German Passport Photo Be?
items: The photo must accurately reflect the applicant’s current appearance and be taken within the last 6 months. If your appearance has changed significantly since the photo was taken, a new photo should be obtained.

sections.title: How Is a German Passport Photo Different From a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: The German passport and the Schengen visa photos share most specifications (35 × 45 mm format, 70–80% face coverage, neutral expression) but differ in the background colour requirement. Depending on the consulate processing the Schengen visa, a white background is required, but the background of a German passport may be only grey. Always check the specific consulate’s current requirements. The digital-only submission rule applies specifically to German identity document applications and does not apply to visa photos submitted on paper. For a Schengen application, the Germany visa photo page prepares the 35 x 45 mm image with the white background.

sections.title: How Much Does a German Passport Photo Cost in 2026?
items: Self-service photo stations (FotoFix, PhotoMe, CEWE) charge €5–€10; pharmacies and drugstores (dm, Müller, Rossmann) and Deutsche Post branches charge €8–€15; a professional studio costs €20–€35+. Bürgeramt self-service terminals charge only a small fee per session. The most affordable option is a reliable online passport photo maker — PhotoGov provides your first digital photo for free, with extra files and services from about €5.

sections.title: Can I Use a Smartphone Selfie for My German Passport Photo?
items: Yes — a smartphone selfie can become a fully compliant image when processed by an online passport-photo maker that applies the official 35 × 45 mm format, grey-background, and face-coverage rules. Keep in mind that for German ID documents, the final transfer to the authority must still happen via a certified photographer’s encrypted QR upload or a Bürgeramt terminal, so the compliant image is used for that upload (or for visa and online applications that accept a supplied file).

sections.title: Are AI-Generated or AI-Edited Passport Photos Allowed in Germany?
items: No. German biometric photos must be a genuine, unaltered photograph of the applicant. The entire digital-submission system was built to prevent image manipulation and morphing, and retouched or filtered images are explicitly rejected. Automatic cropping, resizing, and neutral lighting or background adjustment are acceptable; generating, beautifying, or otherwise digitally altering the face is not.

sections.title: How Long Is the Digital Photo QR Code Valid?
items: The official specification does not set a separate expiry for the QR code beyond the general rule that the photo must reflect your current appearance, for which a photo taken within the last 6 months is recommended. Use the QR code at your Bürgeramt appointment promptly, and obtain a new photo if your appearance changes significantly.

sections.title: Can I Smile in a German Passport Photo?
items: No. The expression must be neutral with the mouth closed and eyes open, looking straight at the camera. Even a slight smile alters facial geometry and can fail the automated biometric check, which is one of the most common reasons for rejection.

requirements/india-visa-photo.h1: India Visa Photo Requirements 2026: How to Make It Right & Avoid Rejection

sections.title: India Visa Photo Requirements 2026: How to Make It Right & Avoid Rejection
items: Planning a trip to India? When applying for a visa, you must upload a compliant photograph that follows all India visa photo requirements — a square image with a plain light-colored or white background, 350 x 350 to 1,000 x 1,000 pixel dimensions with the head measuring 1 to 1-3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm) from chin to hairline, saved as a JPEG of 10 KB – 1 MB for an e-Visa and
10 – 300 KB for a regular visa.
This Guide covers all India visa photo requirements for 2026, so you can submit your application successfully. Have a nice trip!
Source: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India

sections.title: 11 Essential India Visa Photo Requirements: a Checklist
items: Indian photo requirements are published on the official visa and e-Visa portal operated by the Bureau of Immigration under India's Ministry of Home Affairs. Specifications in the table below apply to the standard online upload for both the regular visa and the e-Visa. Follow them exactly: a file that misses one or more official specs may get automatically rejected by the portal.
Requirement
Details
1. File Format
JPEG only.
2. File Size
10 KB – 1 MB for an e-Visa application; 10 – 300 KB for a regular visa application.
3. Photo Dimensions
4. Background
Plain light colored or white background.
5. Framing
Full-face, front view, centered in the frame, showing the entire head from the top of the hair to the bottom of the chin.
6. Head Size
The head must measure 1 to 1-3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm), from the bottom of the chin to the top of the hair.
7. Facial expression
Neutral facial expression. Eyes open, mouth closed.
8. Glasses
The official eVisa website requires a photo "without spectacles."
9. Headwear and accessories

Remove any headwear and accessories obstructing facial features or fully covering your neck (scarf). Only medical (with a relevant letter from a medical provider) or religious headwear worn daily is accepted.
10. Lighting
Even, shadow-free lighting on the face and background — no shadows, textures, glare, or reflections.
11. Borders, frames, decorative artefacts
The photo must be cropped to the edge — no frames, borders, or any decorative elements are allowed.

sections.title: Acceptable Indian Visa Photo Examples
Unacceptable Indian Visa Photo Examples
India Visa Photo Size and Pixel Dimensions Explained
items: India visa photo is a digital upload — its size is measured in pixels. The regular visa instructions on the official visa portal require photos of a minimum of 350 x 350 pixels and a maximum of 1,000 x 1,000 pixels. A rectangular crop, even a photo that is just a few pixels off square, will fail the upload check.

The head, measured from the bottom of your chin to the top of your hair, needs to fill 1 to 1-3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm). Standing too close to the camera pushes the head measurement over the limit; standing too far back leaves too much background, making the face too small for biometric identification. The best way to shoot a proper photo is to stand about three feet away from the camera, placed on a tripod at eye level.

sections.title: India e-Visa vs Regular Visa Photo Requirements: What's Different
items: Most travelers apply for an Indian visa through the e-Visa system. It covers tourist, business, medical, conference, and several other short-stay categories entirely online. A smaller group of applicants, mainly those filing for employment, student, journalist, or research visas, use the regular (sticker) visa route instead. Initially, the application is submitted via the official visa portal too, but it requires a printed application submitted through an Indian mission or its outsourced visa partner. The photo file, therefore, must follow a slightly different set of requirements.

If you already have a compliant e-Visa photo and later need to switch to a regular visa application, check the file size again before you resubmit it. A photo saved at 800 KB clears the e-Visa limit but is too large for the regular visa upload: you would need to compress it before the portal accepts it.

sections.title: India Visa Photo Background, Lighting, and Framing Rules
items: The official Indian visa portal requires a plain light-colored or white background with even lighting on the face and background, free of shadows. The framing instructions ask for a front-facing headshot, with the full head visible from the top of the hair to the bottom of the chin. A tilted head, a photo taken from slightly above or below eye level, or a stray white frame left in by an editing app are all common reasons for rejection.

sections.title: India Visa Photo Rules: Glasses and Facial Expression
items: On the official Indian visa portal, glasses are explicitly addressed only for the e-Visa, where the instructions require the photo to be taken "without spectacles." We recommend following the same rule for a visa sticker application too — it's the safer choice, since even prescription glasses with clear lenses can produce glare or reflections that interfere with biometric identification.

The international rule for facial expression in ID photos is set by the International Civil Aviation Organization Document 9303. It requires a neutral facial expression with both eyes open and mouth closed. Exaggerated expressions, including a wide smile, can compromise the biometric scans. Therefore, when making an Indian visa photo, maintain a calm, natural expression — it keeps your photo consistent both for automated identification systems and border officers.

According to international visa photo standards, all head coverings must be taken off, unless worn for religious or medical reasons. If you wear a religious head covering daily, keep your full face visible from the bottom of your chin to the top of your hairline, following the general framing rule. Check with your Indian mission or the eVisa Help Desk at indian-evisa@gov.in or at +91 82 7808 7808 beforehand if you have a specific concern.

sections.title: India Visa Photo Rules for Children and Infants
items: Every applicant, including an infant, needs their own visa and their own photo. The portal applies the same specifications to every applicant regardless of age. So, a child's photo follows the same file format, size, background, and framing rules as an adult's.

The practical challenge is getting an infant or toddler to sit still, front-facing, with both eyes open, against a plain background. When taking a photo of your infant at home, lay them on a plain light-colored sheet or blanket and photograph from directly above, with the camera level and the baby's face centered in the frame. For a baby who can sit up, a car seat or high chair pushed against a bare wall works, keeping straps, hands, and toys clear of the final crop. Take a longer sequence of shots, twenty or more, and pick the sharpest frame with both eyes open and fingers clear of the face.

sections.title: Where to Apply for an India Visa Photo: e-Visa Portal and Missions Abroad
items: The e-Visa application, including the photo upload, is completed entirely on indianvisaonline.gov.in . The Bureau of Immigration has issued a public advisory naming it as the only correct website for the e-Visa, after several lookalike sites were found copying the government's design to collect fees and personal documents from applicants. Before you upload an Indian visa photo, check that the address bar reads indianvisaonline.gov.in exactly.

A regular visa application starts on the same portal, but the printed form, photo, and passport are then submitted in person or through an outsourced visa application center that handles document collection for Indian missions in the United States and elsewhere. If a visa center or a travel agent quotes you a photo rule that conflicts with what is published on the government portal, the portal is the version that governs your application.

The Bureau of Immigration has also stated plainly that "Government of India has not authorized any agent or intermediary to charge any fee for facilitation of emergency / express Visa/eVisa." A third party can help you fill out paperwork, though the Bureau of Immigration alone sets the rules for your visa timeline and the photo specifications.

sections.title: How to Take an India Visa Photo at Home: 5 Easy Steps
items: A home setup is enough to produce a compliant India visa photo:

Place your phone on a tripod against a light-colored or white wall, preferably by the window. Take the photo in daylight only. Always use the rear camera on your phone for sharper detail than the front-facing one typically captures. Set up a timer.
Remove your glasses, heavy accessories, and non-medical or non-religious headwear.
Stand about three feet from the wall, keep a neutral expression looking directly into the camera.
Take a few shots and choose the best one for your Indian visa.

Use a reputable online tool to create an application-ready photo. For example, PhotoGov's India visa photo maker automates the cropping and background steps: it resizes your uploaded selfie to a square file, checks the pixel dimensions against the range published on indianvisaonline.gov.in, and adjusts the background color. The tool creates a ready-to-submit digital file of the right size, crop, and dimensions that you can download in under 30 seconds.

sections.title: Common Reasons an India Visa Photo Gets Rejected

sections.title: How to Check Your India Visa Photo Before You Submit
items: Since the photo is uploaded as part of the online application, the only real test is whether the file passes the portal's own checks on the first try. Before you upload, confirm the file is a JPEG, is square, falls within the 350 x 350 and 1,000 x 1,000 pixel range, and is sized 10 KB to 1 MB for eVisa and 10 KB to 300 KB for a regular visa. The background must be white or light-colored, and the image must be free of shadows, glare, and textures. You must face the camera directly with a neutral expression, mouth closed and eyes open. To be sure, use a reliable online visa photo checker.

sections.title: Your India Visa Photo Is Ready: What's Next?
items: Your India visa photo is ready. Before you submit your application, here's what to check next.

Review the rest of your application. The photo is only one requirement — make sure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended date of entry, your application form is complete, and any supporting documents are ready to upload.

Check if other Indian documents need a photo too. If you're also applying for an Indian passport, the photo standard is different — see PhotoGov's guide to Indian passport photo requirements for the separate 35×45 mm specification.

Applying for another country as well? Photo specs vary by destination. PhotoGov helps you create submission-ready US visa photo , Canadian visa photo , Schengen visa photo , and many more — each automatically adjusted to current official requirements.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What Size is an Indian Visa Photo?
items: The Indian visa photo must be square, between 350 x 350 and 1,000 x 1,000 pixels, with the head measuring 1 to 1-3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm) from chin to hairline.

sections.title: What is the File Size Limit for an India e-Visa Photo?
items: Between 10 KB and 1 MB. A regular (non-e-Visa) application requires a smaller range of 10 KB to 300 KB — always double-check the official source ( indianvisaonline.gov.in ) before applying.

sections.title: Can I Wear Glasses in My India Visa Photo?
items: No. The official e-Visa instructions specifically require the photo to be taken "without spectacles," and we recommend following the same rule for a regular (sticker) visa.

sections.title: What Color is the Background for Indian Visa Photo?
items: A plain light colored or white background, evenly lit and free of shadows on the face or the background. A light gray or pale wall is acceptable as long as it is even and free of texture.

sections.title: How Recent Must My India Visa Photo Be?
items: Use a current photo that matches your appearance at the time of application, and check for an exact requirement with your Indian mission for your visa category.

sections.title: Do I Need to Submit a Printed Photo, or is Digital Enough?
items: For an Indian e-Visa, you must submit your photo online — so only a digital photo. For a regular visa, the photo is uploaded to the same portal, and the printed application is then submitted through an Indian mission or a third-party visa center.

sections.title: Do the Same India Visa Photo Rules Apply to Children?
items: Yes. The Bureau of Immigration applies the same Indian visa photo specifications to every applicant regardless of age, so a child's photo follows the same format, size, background, and framing rules as an adult's — plain light-colored or white background, 350 x 350 to 1,000 x 1,000 pixels, head measuring 1 to 1-3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm) from chin to hairline, saved as a JPEG of 10 – 300 KB for a regular visa or up to 1 MB for an e-Visa.

sections.title: What File Format is Required for an Indian Visa Photo?
items: JPEG only. The Indian visa upload will reject PNG, HEIC, and other digital photo formats, so make sure you’re creating the right file. If you don’t know how to convert your Android or iPhone photo into a JPEG, use PhotoGov’s India Visa Maker — the tool will automatically prepare an application-ready JPEG with the right proportions and digital file specs.

sections.title: Do e-Visa and Regular India Visa Photos Share the Same Requirements?
items: Yes and no. Both an eVisa and a regular Indian visa require a square photo within a 350 x 350 to 1,000 x 1,000 pixel limit, taken against a white or light-colored background and saved as a JPEG. But the file size for a photo upload differs: 10 KB to 1 MB for the e-Visa, and 10 KB to 300 KB for the regular visa.

sections.title: Why Does My Indian Visa Photo Keep Getting Rejected on Upload?
items: The most common causes for Indian visa photo rejection are:
A non-square crop falling outside the 350 x 350 to 1,000 x 1,000 pixel range A file outside the size limit of 10 – 300 KB for a regular visa or up to 1 MB for an e-Visa
Non-white or non-light-colored background
Shadows or textures in the background
Applicant wears glasses
Non-religious headwear.
Check each item against the checklist in this guide before you reapply.

sections.title: Is indianvisaonline.gov.in the Only Official Site for an India Visa Photo?
items: Yes. The Bureau of Immigration’s only official website is indianvisaonline.gov.in . Do not try to apply for an Indian visa through any other commercial websites.

sections.title: Can I Use the Same Photo for My Indian Visa and my Passport?
items: No. We don’t recommend doing so, as each document type has specific requirements. However, if you’re using online photo-making tools to create a photo for your document, you can use one source image if it’s of sufficient quality.

sections.title: What is the Difference Between an India Visa Photo and an Indian Passport Photo?
items: An India visa photo and an Indian passport photo are part of applications for two completely different documents, issued by different authorities. An India visa photo is submitted by a foreign national applying to enter India; it must be square, sized between 350×350 and 1,000×1,000 pixels. An Indian passport photo, on the other hand, is submitted by an Indian citizen to Passport Seva, following a 35×45 mm photo size and a different set of requirements — you can learn them from our detailed Indian passport photo requirements guide.

requirements/indian-pan-card-photo.h1: Indian PAN Card Photo Requirements in 2026 — New 3.5 x 4.5 cm Rules

sections.title: Indian PAN Card Photo Requirements in 2026 — New 3.5 x 4.5 cm Rules
items: Applying for a Permanent Account Number (PAN) in India and unsure which photo belongs on the form? Prepare two matching recent colour photographs in the 3.5 x 4.5 cm (35 × 45 mm) format, both taken against a plain white background. One photo must present your signature or a left-thumb impression across the edge; the second stays clear — it’s the portrait that will be printed on your PAN card. This format serves other applications too: an Indian passport size photo 35x45 mm can be prepared with our online maker.

This guide takes you through every current PAN card photo requirement, from size and background to placement, signing and submission, with direct links to the official forms and authorised application channels .

sections.title: Indian Permanent Account Number Card Photo Explained
items: A Permanent Account Number, or PAN, is a ten-character alphanumeric identifier issued by India’s Income Tax Department. If you are applying as an individual, the form asks for two matching photographs, and each print does a different job. The left image links your signature or left-thumb impression to the application, while the right image supplies the portrait reproduced on the PAN card. Travel documents use other specifications: an India e visa photo is prepared in the 2 x 2 inch format on a separate page.

The left-hand box of the form is for the photo crossed by your signature or left-thumb impression, with the mark continuing onto the form. The right-hand box is for your portrait to be used on the card.

The form you will use for PAN application depends on your citizenship. Indian citizens apply on Form No. 93 , while applicants who hold another citizenship use Form No. 95 . Applications can be filed online through Protean eGov or UTIITSL , or in person at an authorised Protean PAN Centre or UTIITSL PAN Centre . Instant e-PAN is a separate Aadhaar e-KYC service and uses the photograph held in the Aadhaar record. Applicants holding OCI status often need an OCI passport photo online as well, in the format that document requires.

sections.title: 12 Key Indian PAN Card Photo Requirements: a Checklist
items: The Income Tax Department sets the current PAN photo rules for individual applicants in the official Form No. 93 and Form No. 95 guidelines. The table below consolidates the full specifications for a clean, correctly attached submission.

1. Applicant scope

2. Number of photos

3. PAN photo size

5. Colour

6. Background

7. Recency

8. Image clarity

9. Attachment method

10. Left photograph

11. Right photograph

12. Thumb-impression authentication

sections.title: Acceptable Indian PAN Card Photos
Unacceptable Indian PAN Card Photos
India’s New PAN Application Photo Rule: What Changed in 2026
items: India introduced a new set of PAN application forms under the Income-tax Rules, 2026. New applications filed from Apr 1, 2026 use Form No. 93 for individual Indian citizens and Form No. 95 for individuals who are citizens of another country.

Current Forms 93 and 95 require two recent colour photos in the 4.5 × 3.5 cm (35 × 45 mm) format. The earlier Form 49A and Form 49AA used the smaller 3.5 × 2.5 cm (35 × 25 mm) format. Use the current 35 × 45 mm size for applications filed under the 2026 rules.

sections.title: How to Submit Photos with Form No. 93 or Form No. 95
items: Use the form that matches your citizenship category: No. 93 if you are a citizen of India, No. 95 if you are a citizen of another country. Each form provides two portrait boxes sized for 4.5 × 3.5 cm prints.
Prepare two matching recent colour photographs with a white background.
Trim each print to 35 × 45 mm.
Apply photo adhesive evenly and place both photographs squarely inside the printed boxes.
Sign or place the left thumb impression across the left photograph so the mark extends onto the form.
Keep the right photograph clean and fully visible.
Place the final signature or left-thumb impression inside the declaration box on the last page.
Arrange official attestation for a left-thumb impression through a Magistrate, Notary Public, Oath Commissioner, or Gazetted Officer, with the official seal and stamp.

Applicants using an online PAN application with a physical-document submission mode follow the acknowledgement instructions shown by the selected service. The acknowledgement carries the photographs, signatures, and supporting documents for dispatch through the stated channel.

sections.title: Indian PAN Card Photo Background: White
items: The current Income Tax Department guidelines specify a white background for both photographs. Use a smooth, evenly lit white surface that creates clear separation around the head, hair, and shoulders.

Stand about one metre in front of the background and direct soft light toward the face. This setup keeps the background bright, the facial features clear, and the skin tone natural. Frame a straightforward head-and-shoulders portrait with the face centred and the camera at eye level.

The official PAN forms focus on identification quality rather than a published biometric head-height percentage. Give the face generous space within the 35 × 45 mm frame while keeping the complete head and upper shoulders visible.

sections.title: Glasses in Indian PAN Card Photos
items: For the clearest result, remove glasses before capture. This keeps both eyes fully visible and prevents lens glare. Tinted lenses, sunglasses, or prescription glasses with heavy frames are generally not allowed on ID photos. If you must wear glasses, make sure they have transparent lenses, and look directly into the camera.

sections.title: Where to Get a Compliant Indian PAN Card Photo in 2026
items: A paper PAN application requires two photo prints. You can prepare the photo at home, using an online photo-making tool, get it done by a professional photographer, at a local photo studio, or use a self-service booth. Other Indian forms use the same 35 x 45 mm portrait, and our page on the Indian driving licence photo size explains the RTO version.

sections.title: How to Prepare a PAN Card Photo with PhotoGov
items: PhotoGov is a convenient option when you don't want to spend time and money on a studio visit. Start with a clear, front-facing smartphone photo taken against a simple light surface. Upload it to PhotoGov and select the 35 × 45 mm Indian PAN Card format.

The tool prepares the white background, crop, and printable layout for the required physical size. Download the finished file and order two identical colour prints at a local print shop. The result is a ready-to-attach pair of photos: the left print receives the signature or thumb impression, and the right one remains clear for the card portrait. Choosing a different document type produces an India passport size photo from the same portrait.

sections.title: Indian PAN Card Photos for Minors
items: The Form No. 93 and Form No. 95 guidelines apply the same photo requirement to every individual applicant, including minors. Prepare two recent colour photographs with a white background in the 4.5 × 3.5 cm format.

Choose a calm moment and photograph the child from directly in front. Use an eye-level camera, even light, a smooth white background, and a frame containing only the child. For a baby, place the infant on a smooth white sheet and hold the camera directly above the face.

A minor’s application uses a Representative Assessee where the form requires one. Complete the photograph and signature or left-thumb impression fields according to the current form, and arrange official attestation when a thumb impression is used.

sections.title: Common Reasons for Indian PAN Card Photo Rejection
items: PAN application review focuses on the form, portrait clarity, photograph placement, and authentication marks. These issues create the highest risk of a deficient submission:
Old 35 × 25 mm format : prepare new 35 × 45 mm prints for the current Form No. 93 or Form No. 95.
Single photograph : attach two matching photographs in the two designated boxes.
Coloured or textured background: use a smooth white background with even illumination.
Soft focus or low contrast: select a sharp portrait with clear facial detail and natural colour.
Staple or clip marks : secure each print with photo adhesive.
Signature placed entirely inside the left image : extend the signature or left-thumb impression across the photo-form boundary.
Mark on the right image : reserve the right photograph as a clean, unobstructed portrait.
Unattested thumb impression : obtain the required official attestation, seal, and stamp.
Crooked or undersized print: trim each photograph precisely and align it squarely within the box.
Portrait that differs from the applicant’s current appearance : use a fresh image that supports immediate identification.

sections.title: What to Do If Your Indian PAN Card Photo Is Rejected
items: A photo-related deficiency usually identifies a practical correction: size, quantity, background, print clarity, attachment, or signature placement. Use the deficiency message as the checklist for a fresh submission.
Identify the exact issue stated by the PAN service or processing authority.
Prepare two fresh 35 × 45 mm colour prints on a white background.
Attach the prints with adhesive and complete the left-photo signature and right-photo clarity check.
Resubmit through the channel stated in the deficiency notice and keep the acknowledgement for tracking.

PhotoGov is an independent service. The Income Tax Department and its authorised PAN service channels make the final acceptance decision. This guide reflects the current official forms and government guidance available for 2026 applications.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What Are the Official Indian PAN Card Photo Requirements?
items: An individual applicant submits two recent colour photos with plain white backgrounds, each in the 3.5 × 4.5 cm (35 × 45 mm) format. Sign or place a left-thumb impression across the left photo and the form. Keep the right photo clear, and fix both prints with photo adhesive.

sections.title: What Is the Indian PAN Card Photo Size in Millimetres?
items: The current PAN card photo size is 35 × 45 mm (4.5 × 3.5 cm).

sections.title: What Is the PAN Card Photo Size in Pixels?
items: At 300 DPI, the PAN size is 413 × 531 pixels. At 600 DPI — 826 × 1062 pixels. The official Forms 93 and 95 specify the physical 35 × 45 mm dimensions, while the pixel setting depends on the print resolution.

sections.title: How Many Photos Are Required for a PAN Card Application?
items: Form No. 93 and Form No. 95 require two matching recent colour photographs for an individual applicant. Both photographs fit the 4.5 × 3.5 cm boxes printed on the form.

sections.title: Does a PAN Card Photo Need a White Background?
items: Yes. The current Income Tax Department filing guidelines specify a white background. Use an evenly lit white surface with clear separation around the applicant’s head and shoulders.

sections.title: Where Do I Sign the PAN Card Photographs?
items: Place the signature or left-thumb impression across the left photograph so one part appears on the image and the other part appears on the form. Preserve the right photograph as a clean portrait. Add the final signature or left-thumb impression inside the declaration box on the last page.

sections.title: Can I Use a Left-Thumb Impression?
items: Yes. The form accepts a left-thumb impression. The impression requires attestation by a Magistrate, Notary Public, Oath Commissioner, or Gazetted Officer under official seal and stamp.

sections.title: Are Glasses Allowed in a PAN Card Photo?
items: The current form uses facial clarity as the eyewear-related quality test. A glasses-free portrait delivers the clearest eye area. Clear everyday glasses also support a usable image when the lenses stay transparent and reflection-free.

sections.title: How Recent Should a PAN Card Photo Be?
items: The official guideline uses the term “recent colour photographs” and sets the practical test as current identification. Use a newly captured portrait that closely matches the applicant’s appearance on the filing date.

sections.title: Do Minors Need PAN Card Photos?
items: Yes. The current guidelines include minors in the two-photo rule. Prepare two recent colour photographs with white backgrounds in the 35 × 45 mm portrait format and complete the Representative Assessee section where applicable.

sections.title: Does Instant e-PAN Require a Photo Upload?
items: Instant e-PAN uses Aadhaar e-KYC and completes identity verification through the Aadhaar record. The service skips a separate scanned photo and signature upload. Eligible applicants receive a valid e-PAN through the online process.

sections.title: Can I Take a PAN Card Photo with a Smartphone?
items: Yes. Use another person to hold the smartphone at eye level, create soft front lighting, and stand against a smooth white background. Save the sharpest portrait, crop it to 35 × 45 mm, and print two matching copies at exact size.

sections.title: How Is a PAN Card Photo Different from an Indian Passport Photo?
items: Both documents use a 35 × 45 mm portrait footprint in the current workflow. The PAN application requires two prints and a specific left-photo signature placement. The Indian passport process follows its own biometric framing and submission rules; review PhotoGov’s Indian passport photo guide for that separate standard.

sections.title: Can I Use the Old 35 × 25 mm PAN Photo Size?
items: The 35 × 25 mm format belongs to the earlier Form 49A and Form 49AA workflow. Current individual applications use the 35 × 45 mm portrait boxes shown on Form No. 93 and Form No. 95.

requirements/malaysia-passport-photo-req.h1: Passport Photo Requirements in Malaysia: the Complete 2026 Guide

sections.title: Passport Photo Requirements in Malaysia: the Complete 2026 Guide
items: Getting a Malaysian passport photo right means understanding a set of rules that differ from most countries. Malaysia uses a 35×50 mm portrait format; the background must be pure white — not cream or off-white. Applicants who submit their passport files at a Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia (JIM) counter inside Malaysia do not need to bring a printed photo at all — their biometric image is captured on-site using JIM's Facial Live Capture system.

This guide explains every official requirement issued by JIM and aligned with ICAO Document 9303, along with the practical details that determine whether you need a printed photo, a digital file, or neither.
Source: Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia (Immigration Department of Malaysia)

sections.title: 11 Essential Passport Photo Requirements in Malaysia: a Checklist
items: All Malaysian International Passport (Pasport Malaysia) applications — whether filed at a domestic JIM counter, an overseas Malaysian Mission, or via the MyOnline Passport portal — must meet these specifications. They are set by Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia in line with ICAO Document 9303 biometric standards. The PhotoGov passport photo generator applies all of these specifications automatically. Visa applicants need a separate file, prepared with our Malaysia visa photo 35x50 mm maker.

sections.title: Acceptable Malaysia Passport Photo Sample
items: A photo that passes a JIM officer check, and the MyOnline Passport portal's automated validator shows a sharp, evenly lit colour image of the applicant alone against a seamless, white background . The full head and upper shoulders fill the frame; the face occupies 25–30 mm of the 50 mm height; both eyes are open and looking at the camera; the expression is neutral with the mouth closed.
Photos that consistently pass JIM review share all of the following characteristics:
Crisp, in-focus colour photograph with even lighting — no shadows on the face or backdrop
Strictly white background across the entire frame
Face centred, head level, both eyes at the same height
Neutral expression: mouth firmly closed, eyes open and naturally relaxed
Hair neatly arranged and away from the face, forehead, eyebrows, and ears
Dark hijab, with the full face visible — from forehead to chin, completely unobstructed
No glasses, earrings, or accessories visible anywhere in the image
Photo taken within 6 months, with no filters applied.

sections.title: Unacceptable Malaysia Passport Photo Sample
items: Below are the most common reasons for passport photo rejections at JIM counters and on the MyOnline Passport portal:
Background that is not pure white — JIM's standard has always required white, but applicants frequently submit cream or off-white backgrounds, mistaking them for 'white enough'. They are not.
Shadows on the face or background — directional lighting, overhead lighting, or a subject standing too close to the background wall all create shadows that fail the biometric check.
Glasses of any kind — frames obstruct the periorbital landmarks used for biometric matching; lenses create glare that distorts iris data.
Visible earrings or hair accessories — alter the head silhouette used for facial geometry analysis.
Hair covering forehead, eyebrows, or ears — reduces the number of biometric landmarks available to facial recognition systems.
A hijab or head covering that casts a shadow across any part of the face, or that is so pale it blends into the white background.
Foreign objects such as parents' hands, toys, pacifiers, etc. on baby's photos.
A smile or any non-neutral expression — changes the distance between facial landmarks and corrupts biometric comparison.
Beauty filters, skin-smoothing, or AI retouching — prohibited because they alter the actual appearance of the subject.
Blurry or pixelated image — biometric landmark detection fails on low-quality images.
Photo older than 6 months — appearance can change; an outdated photo reduces matching accuracy.

sections.title: Do You Need to Bring a Photo? How the JIM System Actually Works
items: This is the question that confuses most first-time Malaysian passport applicants — and the answer is different depending on where you apply. Malaysia operates a tiered photo submission system that most other countries do not have.

sections.title: At a JIM Counter Inside Malaysia: No Photo Required
items: For any passport application submitted in person at a domestic Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia office, you do not need to bring a printed photograph. JIM counters across all states use the Facial Live Capture (FLC) system — a calibrated biometric camera operated by JIM staff that captures your photo on-site in a single controlled session. The image is saved directly to your application record in the JIM system. Because the backdrop, lighting, and camera are standardised, technical compliance is guaranteed.

What you are responsible for is presenting yourself correctly: no glasses on your face, no large or face-obscuring accessories, hair away from the face, and a hijab (if worn) in a dark colour, with the full face visible. A JIM officer will ask you to adjust anything that does not comply before the capture.

sections.title: On the MyOnline Passport Portal: A Digital File That Must Pass the Automated Check
items: The MyOnline Passport portal requires a digital photo upload during the online application. The portal's automated validator checks resolution (minimum 413×591 pixels), background colour (white only), and basic ICAO facial alignment. If the photo fails, the application cannot proceed until a passing image is uploaded.

Two things to know: first, the portal has a tick-box for applicants wearing a head covering — use it, or the system may flag your photo purely based on the coverage before a human can review it. Second, a photo taken on a smartphone with portrait mode enabled often fails because the background-blur effect makes the white wall appear graduated rather than uniformly white. Turn portrait mode off before shooting.

sections.title: At an Overseas Malaysian Mission: One Printed Photo Required
items: Malaysians applying at an overseas embassy, High Commission, or consulate must bring one printed colour photo sized at exactly 35×50 mm on photo-quality paper. The same content rules apply. Check the specific mission's website: some missions specify they need two prints; the majority require one.
Which channel needs which format:
Domestic JIM counter → No photo needed; captured on-site by FLC biometric system
MyOnline Passport portal → 1 digital JPEG, minimum 413×591 pixels, white background
Overseas Malaysian Mission → 1 (sometimes 2) printed 35×50 mm colour photo

sections.title: Photographing Babies and Children for a Malaysian Passport
items: Parents often underestimate how different the rules are for young children, and what exceptions JIM actually allows by age group.

sections.title: Newborns and Infants Under 1 Year
items: Newborns can be photographed lying flat on a plain white sheet, with the camera positioned directly overhead so that the entire frame shows only the baby's face and the white surface. This overhead angle eliminates the background shadow problem that makes upright infant photos so difficult. Alternatively, a parent can hold the baby upright from behind — both hands must remain completely out of the frame.

Eyes do not need to be fully open. The mouth may be open or closed. No pacifiers, feeding bottles, toys, or supporting props of any kind may be visible. Dress the baby in dark-coloured clothing — a dark top or bib helps the face stand out clearly against the white background.
At domestic JIM counters, a trained officer will manage the infant capture. Parents should bring the baby well-rested and fed to increase the chance of a calm, cooperative session.

sections.title: Children Aged 1 to 5
items: For this age group, JIM does not strictly require a neutral expression or direct gaze, but the face must be clearly visible and centred in the frame. The background must be plain white with no shadows. No other person, toy, or object may appear in the image. If taking the photo at home, have a second adult gently guide the child's attention to the camera while the photo is taken.

sections.title: Children Aged 6 to 17
items: From age 6, every adult rule applies without exception: neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open and directed at the camera, no glasses, no visible accessories, white background. For children who wear a hijab, the full facial oval must be clearly visible, and the covering must be dark-coloured. Photos must be taken within 6 months of the application.

sections.title: Where to Get a Compliant Malaysian Passport Photo
JIM State Offices: The Easiest Option for Domestic Applicants
items: Every JIM state immigration office — Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Shah Alam, Penang, Johor Bahru, Kota Kinabalu, Kuching, and all district offices — operates the Facial Live Capture system. If you are applying in Malaysia, simply show up, and the photo is handled for you. Appointment slots are available at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my .

sections.title: Photo Studios and Pharmacies for Printed Photos
items: If you need a printed 35×50 mm photo for an overseas mission, photography studios and selected pharmacies across Malaysia offer this service. Watson's and Guardian branches in Klang Valley shopping centres (Mid Valley Megamall, Sunway Pyramid, NU Sentral, IOI City Mall) typically offer walk-in passport photo printing. Independent photo studios in Petaling Jaya, Penang Georgetown, and Johor Bahru are also reliable. Cost: RM 5–20. Always ask for the 35×50 mm Malaysian passport size — not the 35×45 mm UK size, which some booths default to.

sections.title: Self-Service Booths in Hypermarkets and Stations
items: Self-service photo booths are available in Mydin hypermarkets, Giant, Aeon, and at KTM Komuter and LRT stations in the Klang Valley. Before paying, confirm the booth is set to Malaysian passport format (35×50 mm). Booths that output a digital code as well as prints are particularly useful for MyOnline Passport portal submissions.

sections.title: PhotoGov Online Passport Photo Maker
items: PhotoGov's online passport photo maker accepts a selfie taken on any smartphone and returns a JPEG cropped to 35×50 mm, white-background-corrected, and sized to the portal's minimum 413×591-pixel requirement. Having a pre-validated digital file reduces the risk of the MyOnline Passport portal stalling your application. The same tool prepares a Malaysia eVisa photo online , for applicants filing through the visa portal.

sections.title: Taking Your Own Malaysian Passport Photo: A Step-by-Step Setup
items: The most common DIY failure points in a Malaysian passport photo are the pale background that reads as cream rather than white, and the hijab that casts a shadow or merges with the background. The setup below eliminates both.
Tape a large white sheet flat and smooth against a plain wall. The sheet must be crease-free — folds create shadow lines that the portal validator detects as background texture.

Position your main light source in front of you, facing your face from the front. Two lamps or a large window on either side of the camera give even, shadow-free illumination. Do not stand with a window or lamp behind you.
Stand at least 1 metre from the white background. At this distance, no body shadow falls onto the white surface behind you.
Set the camera at eye level. Use a tripod or ask someone to take the shot. Frame your full head and upper shoulders — do not crop the top of the head.
Remove all glasses, earrings, and accessories. Turn off portrait mode, beauty mode, and any AI enhancement on your phone camera.

If you wear a hijab: choose your darkest available one. Black is ideal. Lay it flat against your face and shoulders so the fabric is smooth and not catching light. Check in a mirror that your full forehead, both cheeks, and chin are clearly visible with no shadow anywhere on the face.
Keep your head level, eyes open, mouth closed, expression neutral. Take at least six shots and review each at full zoom for sharpness.

Upload the sharpest, most evenly lit shot to PhotoGov. The tool sets the background to pure white, crops to 35×50 mm, and outputs a compliant JPEG ready for the MyOnline Passport portal, or a print file for overseas mission submissions.

sections.title: 12 Reasons Malaysia Passport Photos Get Rejected — and How to Fix Each Issue
items: Knowing not just what the rule is, but why the specific photo fails, helps you fix the problem on the first retry. Here are the 12 most common rejection reasons with their root causes:
Wrong photo size , not 35×50 mm: the most common mistake. Even slight deviations from the correct size will cause a photo rejction.
Cream, grey, or off-white background : visually similar to white under regular lighting, but detected as non-white by the portal's colour-luminance check.
Shadow on background from standing too close to the wall: standing less than 1 metre from the background causes your shadow to appear behind you, creating a non-compliant photo.
Shadow under chin from overhead or uplighting : use front-facing, diffuse light from both sides.
Glasses: any glasses should be removed for a Malaysian passport photo.
Large accessories, obstructing the face or your silhouette : a scarf covering the neck, large earrings, piercings that alter your natural look, and a full-face view must be removed.
Hair over the forehead or eyebrows : tie back loose hair or clip it away before taking the photo.
Light-coloured hijab blending with background : the silhouette merges with the white background, erasing the border between your silhouette and the background.
Portrait mode : blurs the edges between the subject and the background. Always turn off portrait mode when making an ID photo.
Beauty filter or skin-smoothing : detected by automated systems as altering natural features. Turn off all image enhancement before shooting.
Photo older than 6 months : check the file metadata date before submitting.
Digital file below 413×591 pixels : Use a modern smartphone or camera with a full resolution setting for taking a photo.

sections.title: If JIM or the Portal Rejects Your Photo
items: At a domestic JIM counter, you will be asked to retake the photo on-site using the FLC system, or to return with a corrected print. At the MyOnline Passport portal, the system identifies the rejection reason and prompts you to upload a replacement. Address the specific reason cited — re-uploading the same image produces the same result.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What Are the Passport Photo Requirements in Malaysia?
items: In Malaysia, passport photos must follow specific dimensions and biometric rules defined by the Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia (JIM) and ICAO standards.
Key requirements:
Size : 35 mm wide × 50 mm long (digital: 413 × 591 pixels at 300 DPI equivalent).
Background : Pure white, evenly lit, without patterns or shadows.
Pose : Full face facing the camera, head level, eyes open, mouth closed, neutral expression.
Head size : Face centred, filling most of the frame (not too small, not cropped).
Glasses : Should be removed; no sunglasses or tinted lenses.
Head coverings : Allowed for religious/medical reasons, but the full face must be clearly visible; dark colours recommended for contrast.
Clothing : No uniforms and no white or near-white tops to avoid blending into the background.
Image quality : Sharp, in focus, natural colour, no filters, no retouching, no visible compression artifacts.
Recency : Photo should be taken within the last 6 months.

sections.title: What Is the Malaysian Passport Photo Size?
items: The Malaysian passport photo size is 35 x 50 millimetres (3.5 × 5.0 cm, or 1 .38 × 1.97 inches).
For digital photos, this dimenstions are 413×591 pixels at an effective resolution of 300 DPI , keeping the same 35×50 mm proportion.
When you create or order a Malaysian passport photo, specify “35×50 mm, 35 mm (width) × 50 mm (height)” so that the file or print matches the required dimensions in both millimetres and pixels.

sections.title: What Background Colour Is Required for a Malaysian Passport Photo?
items: For Malaysian passport photos, the background must be a solid, pure white colour with no shadows, patterns, textures, or gradients. Any off‑white, cream, grey, or coloured background (including blue) can cause the photo to be rejected, so always use a clean, uniform white backdrop.

sections.title: How Recent Must a Malaysian Passport Photo Be?
items: A Malaysian passport photo must be taken within the last 6 months before the date you submit your application. This 6‑month validity rule helps ensure that your appearance in the photo still accurately matches how you look at the time of processing.

sections.title: What Is the Digital Size for a Malaysian Passport Photo, and Where Is It Used?
items: For Malaysian passport applications, the digital photo size commonly used is 413×591 pixels , which corresponds to a 35×50 mm photo at an effective 300 DPI and keeps the correct passport aspect ratio.

This digital size is primarily used when you submit your application online (for example, via Malaysian immigration or visa e‑services), where you must upload a compliant JPEG file instead of providing only printed photos.

sections.title: Can You Smile in a Malaysian Passport Photo?
items: No. ICAO biometric standards, which JIM follows, require a neutral expression. A smile changes the position of the cheeks, the shape of the lips, and the partial closure of the eyes — all of which affect biometric landmark mapping. Keep your mouth firmly closed, your jaw relaxed, and your eyes naturally open.

sections.title: What Is the Malaysia Passport Photo Blue Background Color Code?
items: Modern Malaysian passport photos use a pure white background , and blue is no longer accepted for standard Malaysian international passports. If you find older or third‑party references to a “Malaysia passport photo blue background color code” , they usually refer to legacy or specific visa/permit photos that required a light blue background , not to current Malaysian passport requirements; for today’s passport applications, you should always use a solid white background instead.

sections.title: I'm Applying at a JIM Counter Inside Malaysia. Do I Need to Bring a Printed Photo?
items: No. Domestic JIM counters use the Facial Live Capture (FLC) biometric system to take your photo on-site. You do not need to bring a printed photograph for a counter application inside Malaysia. However, you must present yourself in compliance with all JIM photo rules: no glasses, no earrings, hair away from the face. If applying at an overseas Malaysian Mission, one printed 35×50 mm colour photo is required.

sections.title: What Colour Hijab Should I Wear in a Malaysian Passport Photo?
items: The darker the better. Black is the safest choice. Dark navy, dark brown, or charcoal are also acceptable. The reason colour matters: the mandatory white background is pure white, and a pale or cream hijab can blend visually into it, making it impossible for JIM's biometric system to cleanly detect the edge of the face. A dark hijab creates a clear contrast line at the jaw and forehead. The full forehead-to-chin, ear-to-ear face oval must be visible and shadow-free regardless of covering colour.

sections.title: Can I Use a Photo Booth Print for the MyOnline Passport Portal?
items: Only if the booth outputs a digital code or file at the correct specifications (JPEG, minimum 413×591 px, white background, 35×50 mm ratio). Photo booth prints are physical — they cannot be uploaded directly to the portal. Some booths provide a digital download code alongside the print. If the booth only provides a printed photo, arrange a separate digital upload through a tool such as PhotoGov.

sections.title: My Child Is 3 Years Old. Do They Need to Look at the Camera?
items: For children under 6, JIM does not strictly require a direct gaze or neutral expression, but the face must be clearly visible and centred in the frame. At a domestic JIM counter, staff are trained to work with young children. For a home photo for an overseas mission application, have a second adult stand just behind the camera and engage the child's attention. Take multiple shots and choose the one where the face is most clearly visible.

sections.title: What File Format and Minimum Resolution Does the MyOnline Passport Portal Accept?
items: The MyOnline Passport portal accepts JPEG (.jpg) format only. The minimum resolution is 413×591 pixels (width × height) at an effective 300 DPI for the 35×50 mm print size. Higher resolution is accepted. The background must be pure white, and no digital editing should have been applied. The portal runs an automated ICAO alignment check on upload.

sections.title: What Is the Difference Between a Malaysian Passport and a MyPR Permit Photo?
items: Malaysian International Passport photos follow the 35×50 mm specification set by Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia. MyPR and long-term pass documents may have separate photo requirements specified by the relevant department at the time of application. Always check the specific documentation checklist provided with each application type. When in doubt, a 35×50 mm white-background ICAO photo is the safest default for any JIM-related document submission.

requirements/nepal-passport-photo.h1: Nepal Passport Photo Requirements: 2026 Rules for Adults and Children

sections.title: Nepal Passport Photo Requirements: 2026 Rules for Adults and Children
items: Applying for or renewing a Nepal passport? Most likely, you don’t need to submit a photograph. For applicants aged 5 or older, the photo is captured live during in-person biometric enrollment. Parents or legal guardians of children under 5 need to submit 2 printed photos measuring 35 x 45 mm (3.5 x 4.5 cm), with a plain white background, and no borders or frames.

This Guide covers all Nepal passport photo requirements in 2026, including the live enrollment process. All information is current and verified against official Nepal government sources in August 2026.
Source: Department of Passports, Nepal

sections.title: 11 Essential Nepal Passport Photo Requirements: a Checklist
items: Nepal passport photo requirements are set by Nepal's Department of Passports (under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and by Nepal's diplomatic missions abroad. Since adult applicants are enrolled in person, most of the information in the table below applies to applications for children under five .
Requirement
Details
1. Who Needs to Submit a Photo
Only parents or legal guardians of children aged under 5 years old must submit printed passport-size photos. For all other applicants, the photo is captured live at the enrollment center.
2. Number of Photos
2 printed photos.
3. Size
4. Face Size
70-80% of the frame, from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head.
5. Background
Plain, white.
6. Print Quality
High resolution, professionally printed, borderless.
7. Eyes and Ears
Both eyes open. Ears visible where possible.
8. Forehead Marks
No tika. A сhild’s photo with a tika on the forehead is not accepted. During biometric capture, applicants are advised to remove tikas too.
9. Recency
The photo must be a current, true likeness of the child.
10. Live Enrollment (Age 5+)
A passport officer captures your photo and biometric data in person at a Department of Passports enrollment center or a Nepali diplomatic mission.
11. Digital Document Uploads
For the online pre-enrollment form, scanned documents are capped at 300 – 400 KB, in JPEG or PNG format, depending on the enrollment center.

sections.title: Do You Need to Submit a Nepal Passport Photo at All?
items: No, if you're an adult. The Department of Passports enrolls every adult applicant in person, and the biometric photo is taken during the appointment (alongside fingerprints and a signature). First, an applicant needs to fill out the online pre-enrollment form, book a slot, and bring documents to the office on the required date. For children under 5, their parents or legal guardians do need to bring two printed passport-size photos for the passport appointment .

sections.title: Acceptable Nepal Passport Photo Examples
Unacceptable Nepal Passport Photo Examples
Nepal Passport Photo Size and Face Position Rules
items: The Nepal passport photo size for children under five is 35 x 45 mm (3.5 x 4.5 cm), and the print must not have borders or frames. The face should fill 70 – 80% of the frame, measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head. These requirements follow the ICAO Document 9303 biometric photo standard for machine-readable and electronic passports worldwide. Nepal

sections.title: Nepal Passport Photo Background, Lighting, and Print Quality
items: Nepal passport photo background must be plain white, with no patterns, textures, or shadows. The photo must be professionally printed from a high-resolution file source. A soft-focus, low-resolution, or visibly pixelated print is treated the same as a photo with the wrong background and will not be accepted.

sections.title: Face, Eyes, and Forehead Marks in a Nepal Passport Photo
items: For all Nepal passport photos — whether captured by the enrollment officer or taken of a child under five — both eyes must be open, and ears should preferably be visible. As with other ID photos, glasses are discouraged; if an applicant must wear them, the lenses must be free of glare or flash reflection, and the eyes must remain fully visible, not obscured by heavy frames or hair.
At in-person biometric appointments, applicants may be asked to remove heavy jewelry and overly bright makeup before their biometrics are captured.

A child’s photo showing a tika — the mark many Nepalis wear on the forehead for religious or festival occasions — is not accepted. For adult applicants and children over 5 years old attending a biometric appointment, it is recommended to remove a tika for the passport photo capture.

sections.title: Nepal Passport Photo Requirements for Children Under 5
items: Children under 5 are the only applicant type that needs to submit a photo. Parents are allowed to complete the process without bringing an infant or toddler in for live biometric enrollment.
All Nepal passport rules — 35 x 45 mm, plain white background, no frames or borders, both eyes open, no tika, professionally printed from a high-resolution source photo — apply for children.
Parents complete the special-provision pre-enrollment form on the Government website from home, and then provide all the paperwork in person.
A minor's passport is valid for 5 years, after which renewal requires a Minor Identity Card.

sections.title: Documents Required With a Child's Nepal Passport Photo
items: Alongside the 2 printed photos, the pre-enrollment form requires:
Child's citizenship or birth registration certificate
Parents' marriage registration certificate
Parents' citizenship certificates
Scans of parents' passport photo pages
Scans of parents’ visa pages (if applying at a mission abroad).

sections.title: How the Nepal e-Passport Application Process Works
items: The process starts online: an applicant fills the pre-enrollment form , selects a 34-page or 66-page passport booklet, selects an enrollment center, and uploads a scanned citizenship certificate or an existing passport scan at 300 – 400 KB (double-check the enrollment center requirements).
The completed form with a barcode and a QR code is downloaded, printed, and brought to the appointment.
At the appointment, an officer verifies the documents, captures an applicant’s photograph, fingerprints, and signature, and completes the live enrollment after the applicant pays the fee.

sections.title: Applying for a Nepal Passport From Abroad
items: The same pre-enrollment form applies, but an applicant books an appointment at a Nepali embassy or consulate. Processing commonly takes around a month from the date of application.

sections.title: What to Bring to Your Nepal Passport Photo Appointment
items: An applicant must bring the printed pre-enrollment form (with QR and barcode), the original citizenship certificate or the minor’s identity card, the current or expired passport, and a fee. If a parent or legal guardian is attending on behalf of a child, they must bring the documents listed in the section above.

sections.title: Common Reasons for Nepal Passport Photo Rejection
items: As most applicants don’t submit a photo, most rejection risks cover the child-under-5 category. We list them in the table below.
Reason for rejection
How to fix it
Background is not plain white
Reshoot against a plain white backdrop with no shadow
Photo has a frame or a border
Use a borderless print, cropped to the edge of the image
Face doesn’t fit within the required 70-80% of the frame range
Reframe so the face fills roughly that share of the photo
Tika visible on the forehead
Reshoot without a tika
Print is blurry, low-resolution, or home-printed
Have the photo professionally printed at proper resolution
Uploaded document exceeds the file size cap, or is in the wrong format
Compress the scan to fit the 300 – 400 KB range and resave it as JPEG or PNG

A wrong background, a border/frame, or an oversized file can usually be fixed with a reprint or a resave. A face that is framed too small or too large, or a photo taken with a tika, needs a full reshoot.

sections.title: Your Nepal Passport Requirements Are Clear: What's Next?
items: Whether you're preparing for live enrollment or getting a child's photo ready, here's what to check next.

Review the rest of your appointment paperwork. The photo is only one piece of the process — make sure your printed pre-enrollment form (with QR and barcode), citizenship certificate or minor's identity card, and current or expired passport are all ready to bring in person.

Applying on behalf of a child under 5? Confirm you have both printed photos plus the child's citizenship or birth registration certificate, the parents' marriage registration certificate, parents' citizenship certificates, and parents' passport photo pages before the appointment.
Applying from abroad? The same pre-enrollment form applies, but book your appointment at a Nepali embassy or consulate instead — processing commonly takes around a month.

Traveling internationally once your passport is issued? Visa photo specs vary by destination. PhotoGov also covers the US visa photo , Canadian visa photo , Schengen visa photo, and many more — each automatically adjusted to the official requirements.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
Do I Need to Submit a Photo for My Nepal Passport?
items: Only if you are applying on behalf of a child under 5. Applicants aged 5 and older have their photo captured live during in-person enrollment and submit nothing beforehand.

sections.title: What Size is a Nepal Passport Photo for a Child Under 5?
items: 35 x 45 mm (3.5 x 4.5 cm), borderless, with the face filling about 70% to 80% of the frame.

sections.title: How Many Photos Do I Need for a Nepal Passport?
items: 2 printed photos, and only for a child under 5. No photos are needed for applicants 5 and older: the biometric photo is taken by the enrollment officer during your passport appointment.

sections.title: Can I Take my Child’s Nepal Passport Photo at Home?
items: Yes. You can take a clear portrait of your child and use an online Nepal passport-making tool like PhotoGov to prepare it for application. All you’ll need to do is print it out at the nearest shop and bring it to the appointment.

sections.title: What Happens During Nepal's Live Photo and Biometric Enrollment?
items: A passport officer takes your photograph, fingerprints, and signature in person at a domestic enrollment center or a Nepali embassy or consulate, as part of the same appointment where your documents are verified.

sections.title: Can I Fix a Mistake in My Photo After My Enrollment Appointment?
items: Only if you catch it during the appointment itself. The Department of Passports states that corrections, including to the photo, can be requested during the capture step, but not once the application has been approved, at which point a new application is required.

sections.title: Can I Wear a Tika in My Nepal Passport Photo?
items: No. A photo with a tika on the forehead is not accepted for newborn, minor, and adult photo submissions alike.

sections.title: Can I Wear Glasses in a Nepal Passport Photo?
items: It is highly recommended to remove glasses for your passport photo, and the lenses may have glare or a flash reflection that may interfere with the biometric identification.

sections.title: Can I Wear a Headscarf, Topi, or Other Head Covering?
items: Yes. But only if it is religious headwear that you officially wear on a daily basis. All other head accessories, hats, and headwear must be removed.

sections.title: How Recent Must a Nepal Passport Photo Be?
items: A photo is taken during the enrollment. For a child under 5, the photo must be current — preferably, take it right before the submission.

sections.title: What File Size and Format Does the Online Pre-Enrollment Portal Accept?
items: Official size limits are 300 KB (official passport portal) and 400 KB (some of the foreign missions). Therefore, we recommend keeping the size at 300 KB.

sections.title: Where do I Apply for a Nepal Passport From Abroad?
items: At your nearest Nepali embassy or consulate, after completing the same online pre-enrollment form used domestically and booking an appointment for live biometric and photo enrollment.

sections.title: What Happens if My Child's Photo Does Not Meet Requirements?
items: The application is sent back for a corrected photo, whether the issue is the background, the border, the face size, or a visible tika. The rest of the pre-enrollment file does not need to be resubmitted, only the photo.

sections.title: How do I Get a Ready Photo for My Child's Nepal Passport Application?
items: Upload a picture to the Nepal passport photo maker , which sizes it to 35 x 45 mm on a plain white background, then have it professionally printed before your enrollment center visit.

requirements/saudi-arabia-evisa-photo.h1: Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Requirements: the Complete 2026 Checklist

sections.title: Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Requirements: the Complete 2026 Checklist
items: Planning a trip and wondering what the Saudi Arabia eVisa photo requirements are in 2026? You must submit one digital photo with a white background at 200 × 200 pixels, file size 5–100 KB, and face taking up 70–80% of the photo (1.4" × 1.6" from chin to crown). The photo must be taken within the past 6 months and submitted online via an eVisa portal. You can produce a Saudi e visa photo 200x200 px from an ordinary selfie with our online maker.

This guide covers all current eVisa photo specifications directly from the official Tourism Website of Saudi Arabia , provides eVisa photo samples, and offers practical tips to help you create an accurate image and avoid application delays or rejections. Residents applying for an Iqama or national ID need a Saudi Arabia ID card photo in the 4 x 6 cm format instead.

sections.title: 10 Essential Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Requirements
items: Saudi Arabia Ministry of Tourism sets the official eVisa specifications, based on the international biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303 . The photo you submit with your eVisa application must follow all 10 specs listed below to avoid delays or rejections.
Parameter
Requirement
1. Number of photos
One identical digital photograph per applicant.
2. Recency
Must be no more than six months old to reflect an applicant’s up-to-date likeness.
3. Size
200 × 200 pixels , square (1:1).
4. Head size
1.4 × 1.6 in from chin to crown, or 70-80% of the shot.
5. File size
5 to 100 KB.
6. Framing
Close-up of the face and top of the shoulders, square in the shot.
7. Background
White , plain, with no pattern and no shadows.
8. Facial expression
Only a neutral facial expression is allowed.
9. Head covering
Not permitted, except for religious or medical reasons. When worn, the face must remain visible from the lower chin to the forehead, with no shadow cast on the face.
10. Eyewear
Preferably removed . If you must wear glasses for medical reasons, make sure that the lenses have zero glare, no tinting, and both eyes fully visible.

sections.title: Saudi eVisa Photos: Special Cases
Head Coverings
items: Headwear is generally not permitted, except for religious head coverings such as hijabs, keffiyehs, and turbans, which are explicitly allowed under official guidance. In these cases, the face must remain fully visible from the chin to the forehead, and the fabric must not cast any shadow across the face.

sections.title: Medical Head Coverings
items: Medical head coverings fall under the same exception category as religious ones, subject to the identical visibility standard: full chin-to-forehead exposure with no shadowing from the covering.

sections.title: Voluminous or Textured Hair
items: For applicants with voluminous or textured hair, the specification requires that the head and hairstyle be shown in full — the photo should not be cropped tightly just to accommodate hair volume. The face-size requirement takes precedence over fitting the entire hairstyle into a tighter frame.

sections.title: Eyewear
items: Remove glasses entirely for the photo. If they must be worn for medical reasons, the frame must not cross the eyes, and there should be no glare or tinting on the lenses.

sections.title: Step-by-Step: How to Upload Your Photo on visa.visitsaudi.com
items: Step 1. Prepare your photo file at exactly 200 × 200 pixels, between 5 and 100 KB, on a plain white background.

Step 2. Create or log in to your account on the eVisa portal and start a new application. Note that the system sends a verification code to your email both at registration and at every subsequent login — you won't be able to access your account without entering it.
Step 3. Enter your passport and personal details, then proceed to the photo upload step.
Step 4. Upload your photo file. The system automatically checks file size and dimensions; a file outside the 5–100 KB range or not sized 200 × 200 px will be rejected before you can continue.
Step 5. Review the preview the portal displays — confirm the face is centered and fills roughly 70–80% of the frame before submitting.

Step 6. Complete payment. The portal adds the applicable visa, digital-service, and insurance-related charges. The insurance premium depends on the selected provider, so check the final amount displayed at checkout. Most applications are approved quickly; check your account or email for confirmation and your linked eVisa.

sections.title: How to Apply for a Saudi Arabia Tourist eVisa
items: The entire application process takes place online through the official portal, visa.visitsaudi.com . You'll need a passport valid for at least six months beyond your planned stay, a digital passport-style photo meeting the specifications above, and a valid payment method for the visa fee.
The official processing estimate ranges from one minute to three business days. The approved eVisa is sent as an email attachment. Carry a copy of it when arriving in Saudi Arabia.

sections.title: Where to Take a Saudi eVisa Photo (and What It Costs)
items: Choose whichever location is most convenient for you, or simply take the photo at home and process it with a reliable online photo-making tool.

Pharmacy photo counters (e.g., CVS, Walgreens) — Widely available and generally familiar with visa-photo formats, but staff often default to producing a standard printed passport photo unless you specifically request a digital file sized to the Saudi eVisa's 200×200-pixel spec.
Professional photo studio — Offers in-person assistance and can deliver a digital file on request. This is typically the most expensive option, and some studios require an appointment in advance.

Online visa photo tool — Purpose-built tools like PhotoGov automatically crop, resize, and compress your photo to the exact 200×200-pixel dimensions and 5–100 KB file size the portal requires, removing the guesswork of manual editing. Note that PhotoGov is free to use in all countries outside the US, UK, and Canada, where affordable pricing applies.
