sections.title: How to Take a Saudi eVisa Photo at Home
items: Setting. Stand far enough in front of the wall to prevent shadows, and position the camera approximately 1.5–2 meters away at eye level. The natural light coming from the front is preferable to overhead lighting or flash, both of which tend to produce the shadows the specification explicitly prohibits.
Position. Face the camera directly with your head square — not turned or tilted — ensuring both ears and cheeks remain visible, in line with the official wording.

Camera. Use a smartphone's rear camera rather than the front-facing selfie camera, since it typically offers better resolution and less distortion. A tripod, or having a second person take the shot, produces a straighter, better-centered result than a handheld photo.

After the shot. Crop the image to a perfect square (1:1 ratio) and resize it to exactly 200 × 200 pixels, then confirm the file size falls between 5 and 100 KB before uploading. Most basic photo editors and free online tools can handle both steps.

sections.title: Visual Do's and Don'ts
items: Do
Don't
Plain white background, no shadows
Off-white, patterned, or shadowed background
Head square to the camera
Head turned, tilted, or in profile
Face filling 70–80% of the frame
Face too small or too tightly cropped
Religious/medical headwear with full face visible
Caps, hats, or sunglasses worn without religious/medical reason
Exactly 200 × 200 px, 5–100 KB
Photo sized for a printed passport photo
Recent photo (within 6 months)
Reused photo from an old application
Both ears and cheeks visible
Side profile or heavily angled shot
Full head and hairstyle shown if hair is voluminous
Tightly cropped photo that cuts off hair to fit the frame

sections.title: Saudi eVisa Photo Requirements for Children
items: The photo requirements for children are the same as for adults, with no exceptions for age. Each child must have an individual photo — 200 × 200 pixels, plain white background, 5–100 KB file size — with no other person in the frame.
No parent's hands, arms, or body may appear in the shot, even partially, and no toys, pacifiers, or props of any kind are allowed.

For infants and toddlers who can't sit or stand independently, laying the child flat on a plain white sheet or blanket and photographing from directly above works well, as long as the background around the face and shoulders stays plain white with no folds or shadows.

sections.title: Why Saudi eVisa Photos Get Rejected — the Most Common Reasons
items: Wrong file dimensions The photo must be exactly 200 × 200 pixels. Photos formatted for a printed passport photo, for example, 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm, do not meet this digital spec and will be rejected.

File size outside the 5–100 KB range A high-resolution photo taken straight from a smartphone is almost always too large and needs compressing first. Overcompressing can also cause problems, pushing the file below 5 KB and triggering rejection at the opposite end of the range.
Off-white or shadowed background Any tint, gradient, or visible shadow behind the applicant violates the "no pattern, no shadows" rule and is one of the most common reasons for rejection.
Head tilted, not square in the shot The specification requires the head to be square to the camera, with both ears and cheeks visible. A side-angled or tilted photo does not meet this standard.
Face too small or too large in frame The face must take 70–80% of the frame. This requirement is most often missed by photographing from too far away or by cropping too tightly.
Non-religious head covering Hats, caps, or sunglasses worn without a religious or medical reason are rejected under the general rule that headwear is not permitted.
Shadow cast by religious headwear Even when a religious head covering itself is allowed, a shadow falling across the face from the fabric can still cause the photo to be rejected.
Outdated photo .A photo older than six months, or one that no longer reflects the applicant's current appearance, does not meet the recency requirement.

sections.title: What to Do If Your Saudi eVisa Photo is Rejected
items: Once you've identified which of the issues above caused the rejection, the fix follows the same basic pattern: correct that specific cause, then retake and re-upload the photo.

If the problem was dimensions or file size, resize the image to exactly 200 × 200 pixels and adjust compression until it falls within 5–100 KB — don't simply crop or shrink the existing file, since heavy compression often degrades image quality and can trigger a second rejection. If the problem was the background, lighting, or head position, retake the photo entirely against a plain white wall with even, front-facing light, keeping the head square to the camera and both ears visible; a poor original is rarely worth salvaging through editing. If the issue was headwear-related — either a non-permitted item or a shadow from religious head covering — adjust the lighting angle or remove the non-permitted item and take a new photo rather than trying to edit shadows out.

Once the corrected photo is ready, upload it through your existing application on the official eVisa portal; there is no separate fee for fixing a photo before final submission. If your eVisa has already been issued and you need a new one for a future trip, you'll need to submit a completely new application, since photos are not carried over between separate applications.

sections.title: The eVisa Requirements are Clear: What's Next?
items: Your Saudi Arabia eVisa photo is ready. Before you submit your application, here's what to check next.

Review the rest of your application. The photo is only one requirement — make sure your passport is valid for at least six months from your intended date of entry, your application form is complete, and any supporting documents are ready to upload.

Check if other Saudi Arabia documents need a photo too. If you're also applying for a standard embassy visa or a work permit, PhotoGov can generate a compliant photo for each in under a minute: Saudi Arabia visa 2×2 in (51×51 mm) , Saudi Arabia work permit 4×6 cm .

Applying for another country as well? Photo specs vary by destination. PhotoGov also covers the US visa photo , Canadian visa photo , Schengen visa photo , and Indian visa photo — each automatically adjusted to the exact requirements.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What is the Saudi Arabia Tourist eVisa Photo Size?
items: The Saudi Arabia tourist eVisa photo must be exactly 200 × 200 pixels, with a file size between 5 and 100 KB. This is a digital-only specification, so a printed passport-style format such as 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm does not meet the requirement. If the file is too large, it must be compressed; if it is too small, it must be re-saved at a slightly higher quality before upload.

sections.title: What Background is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo?
items: The background must be plain white, with no pattern, no visible texture, and no shadows behind the applicant. Even a slight tint or a soft gradient can cause the photo to be rejected, so lighting matters as much as the backdrop itself. For the cleanest result, use even front-facing light and avoid flash or overhead lighting.

sections.title: How Recent Must a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Be?
items: The photo must have been taken within the last six months and should reflect the applicant’s current appearance. Older images are a common reason for rejection, especially if the haircut, facial hair, or general appearance has changed. A recent photo also reduces the risk of the upload being flagged as outdated during review.

sections.title: What Head Size is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa?
items: The face should occupy 70–80% of the image, measured from the chin to the crown. In practice, this means the photo should be a close-up of the face and upper shoulders, not a full bust shot and not an overly tight crop. If the face is too small, the image looks distant; if it is too large, the head may be cut off, or the framing may fail the specification.

sections.title: What Facial Expression is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo?
items: The expression must be neutral, with the face looking directly at the camera. Smiling broadly, opening the mouth, or making an exaggerated expression can lead to rejection because the photo must show a natural, standard passport-style likeness. The safest approach is a relaxed face with a closed mouth and open eyes.

sections.title: Can I Wear Glasses in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo?
items: Glasses are best removed unless they are medically necessary. The official rules focus on clear visibility of the face, and glasses can create glare, reflections, or partial eye obstruction, which may lead to rejection. If glasses must remain on, the lenses should be completely clear with both eyes fully visible, and the frame should not cover the eyes.

sections.title: Can I Wear a Hijab or Other Religious Head Covering in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo?
items: Yes. Religious head coverings are allowed as an explicit exception to the general no-headwear rule. The face still has to remain fully visible from chin to forehead, and the fabric must not cast any shadow across the face. The same principle applies to medical head coverings.

sections.title: Can I Wear Non-Religious Headwear in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo?
items: No. Hats, caps, fashion headwear, and sunglasses are not permitted unless the covering is worn for religious or medical reasons. Even then, the face must stay fully visible, and the covering must not interfere with the lighting or framing. If there is any doubt, the safest choice is to remove it.

sections.title: Is the Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Digital or Printed?
items: The tourist eVisa uses a digital upload only. The image is submitted through the online application system, and no printed photo is required for the standard tourist route. That means the file must meet both the visual requirements and the technical file-size and pixel-dimension rules before submission.

sections.title: Can I Use a Printed Passport-Style Photo for a Saudi Arabia eVisa?
items: No. Printed passport formats such as 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm are not the same as the eVisa’s digital requirement. The portal is designed for uploading a digital file, so an image prepared for a print workflow will need to be properly resized and reformatted first. You can use PhotoGov to create an eVisa-ready photo in under a minute.

sections.title: What Happens if a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo File is Outside the 5–100 KB Range?
items: The upload will fail, and the file will need to be corrected before it can be submitted. A smartphone image straight from the camera is often too large, while an overcompressed image can fall below the minimum size. The safest fix is to adjust the file properly before re-uploading, rather than trying to force an incorrect file through the portal.

sections.title: What Rules Apply to Infant Saudi Arabia eVisa Photos?
items: Infants must still be photographed alone, with no other people, hands, toys, or props visible in the frame. The image should show the child clearly against a plain white background, with the face centered and lighting kept even. If the child cannot sit upright, a flat white surface can be used as long as the final image remains clean and compliant.

sections.title: Do I Need a New Saudi eVisa Photo for Every Trip?
items: No. A Saudi tourist eVisa is normally valid for one year and permits multiple entries, unless otherwise stated on the issued visa. You do not need to submit a new application or photo for each trip while the eVisa and the passport used for the application remain valid. Always check the validity and entry conditions shown on your issued eVisa.

sections.title: How Should a Rejected Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Be Fixed?
items: Identify the exact issue that caused the rejection, then correct it and upload a new file through the same application. If the problem is technical, such as size or dimensions, resize and re-save the image; if the problem is visual, such as lighting, framing, or headwear, retake the photo. The best results usually come from starting with a fresh image rather than trying to rescue a flawed one.

requirements/schengen-visa-photo-require.h1: Schengen Visa Photo Requirements: Official 2026 Guide, Expert Verified

sections.title: Schengen Visa Photo Requirements: Official 2026 Guide, Expert Verified
items: A Schengen visa photo is a biometric image required by the embassies and consulates of all 29 Schengen Area member states when processing short-stay visa (type C) and long-stay national visa (type D) applications. The photo must be 35 × 45 mm , taken against a plain white, off-white, or light-coloured background , within the past six months , showing the applicant's full face with a neutral expression. These specifications apply to citizens of all nationalities applying at any Schengen embassy worldwide.
This 2026 guide covers every official Schengen photo requirement you need to follow to prevent delays or rejection of your short-stay or long-stay visa application.

sections.title: 12 Essential 2026 Schengen Visa Photo Requirements: Checklist
items: Schengen visa photo specifications are harmonized across all 29 member states. The photograph must comply with the biometric standards set by the European Union Visa Code ( Regulation EC No 810/2009 ) and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 , ensuring consistent automated facial recognition across all Schengen member states.

All embassies, consulates, and visa application centers process photos according to the same unified rules listed below. You don't need to verify specifications country by country — the requirements are identical whether you apply for a French, German, Italian, Spanish, or any other Schengen member-state visa.
Specification
Official Requirement
1. Number of Photos

Two identical printed photographs are required for most paper-based Schengen visa applications. Online application portals for specific member states usually accept a single digital upload ; always confirm the exact count in the instructions provided by the applying embassy or visa center.
2. Recency

The photo must be taken within the last six months and accurately reflect your current appearance. A significant change — such as new facial hair, post-surgery changes, or weight loss — requires a fresh photo even if the previous one is still within the six-month window.
3. Schengen Visa Photo Size

35 × 45 mm . The face must occupy 70–80% of the image height : the head from chin to crown should measure 32–36 mm . The eye line must be positioned between 25 and 35 mm from the bottom edge of the photo. This is the standard EU/ICAO biometric portrait format.
4. Color
Only full-color photographs are accepted. The image must reproduce natural skin tones and hair color accurately. Black-and-white, sepia, or color-filtered photos are not permitted.
5. Background

Plain white, off-white, or very light grey background only , free of shadows, patterns, gradients, textures, or objects. Some member-state guidance specifies pure white; in practice, a uniform off-white or very pale grey (lighter than the face) is also accepted. Avoid cream, warm beige, or blue-tinted backgrounds.
6. Lighting

Even, diffuse illumination with no harsh shadows under the nose, chin, or around the ears. No flash glare, red-eye, or bright patches on the forehead. Natural window light or soft studio lighting produces the best results.
7. Positioning and Framing
The applicant must face the camera directly , with the head centered horizontally and vertically in the frame. No tilting, turning, or angling. Shoulders must be visible and squared to the camera.
8. Facial Expression

A natural, neutral expression is mandatory: both eyes open and fully visible, mouth closed, no smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, or squinting. Biometric facial recognition systems require relaxed facial muscles for accurate measurement.
9. Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Everyday clothing in solid colors is recommended. Uniforms, military camouflage, and clothing that blends with the white background are not allowed. Head coverings are permitted only for documented religious or medical reasons and must not obscure the hairline, forehead, eyebrows, or any part of the face.
10. Glasses

Prescription glasses are accepted if the lenses don’t have glare or flash reflections and the frames don’t cover the eyes — the eyes must be fully visible. Tinted lenses, photochromic lenses, and sunglasses are never allowed. Some consulates prefer no glasses at all, so removing them is the safest option.
11. Headphones and Electronic Devices
All earphones, earbuds, and wireless headsets must be removed before the photograph is taken. Medically necessary hearing aids that are small and do not obstruct facial features may be worn.
12. Print and Digital Quality

Printed photos must be produced on professional photo paper (matte or glossy finish) with no borders, perforations, staple holes, or ink marks. No “pearl or silkscreen effect” is allowed, according to ICAO. Digital photos submitted online must be in JPEG format , 413 × 531 pixels (or 600 × 771 px) at 300 DPI for the standard 35×45 mm format, and a maximum of 10 MB in file size, with no visible compression artifacts, pixelation, or digital retouching.

sections.title: Acceptable Schengen Visa Photo Examples
items: A compliant Schengen visa photo shows the applicant's full face centered against a clean white or very light background. The image is sharp and evenly lit, with no shadows on the face or the backdrop. The subject maintains a neutral expression — both eyes fully open, mouth closed, and facial muscles relaxed. The head occupies approximately 70–80% of the frame height. No glasses, hats, or non-religious accessories are present.

sections.title: Unacceptable Schengen Visa Photo Examples
items: Common non-compliant photos include: images with a colored or patterned background; photos where the subject is smiling or squinting; shots with visible glasses or sunglasses; photos taken more than six months ago; images with shadow across the face or a bright flash spot on the forehead; and photos where the head occupies less than 70% of the frame.

sections.title: Digital vs. Printed Schengen Visa Photos Explained
items: For most Schengen visa applications, two identical printed photographs must be submitted together with the application form. However, a growing number of member-state consulates and centers also accept or require a single digital photo upload for preliminary processing. The biometric specifications remain identical for both formats.

A printed Schengen visa photo must be exactly 35 × 45 mm , professionally printed on matte or glossy photo paper, with no borders or frames. A digital file prepared for upload or for use as a print source must be a JPEG at 300 DPI , with a pixel dimension of at least 413 × 531 pixels (equivalent to 35 × 45 mm at 300 DPI). File size must not exceed 10 MB .

sections.title: How to Take a Schengen Visa Photo at Home
items: Taking your Schengen visa photo at home is straightforward with a modern smartphone and good natural light. Follow these steps, then upload your image to PhotoGov for automatic resizing, background correction, and compliance verification.

Set up the right lighting. Position yourself facing a window or other soft light source. The illumination should be even across your face — no shadows under the nose or chin, no bright patches on your forehead. Avoid using an on-camera flash directly in front of your face.

Prepare a plain background. Stand or sit in front of a plain white wall, a white door, or hang a white sheet. The background should have no visible patterns, textures, or shadows. If you cannot find a perfectly white surface, PhotoGov's background correction tool will adjust it automatically after upload.

Use a tripod or ask for assistance. Position the camera at eye level, approximately 1–1.5 meters (3–5 feet) away. If taking the photo yourself with a front camera, hold the phone at arm's length and ensure it is level with your face to avoid distortion.

Frame and position correctly. Your head and shoulders should both be visible. Look directly into the lens, keep your head level and straight, and maintain a calm, neutral expression — eyes open, mouth closed.
Take multiple shots and select the sharpest one. Do not apply any filters, beauty modes, or retouching before uploading. PhotoGov performs all necessary adjustments to meet official specifications.

The tool will crop the image to the required 35 × 45 mm format, scale the head to 70–80% of the frame, correct the background, and validate all technical parameters. sections.title: Schengen Visa Photo for Children
items: Children, including infants, must submit Schengen visa photos that meet the same biometric specifications as adult photographs: 35 × 45 mm dimensions, plain white or off-white background, neutral expression, and taken within the past six months. No exceptions are made for children over the age of approximately 12 months.

For infants under one year old, certain practical exceptions apply: the baby's eyes may be partially closed, and a slight mouth opening is generally accepted. Infants may be photographed lying on a plain white blanket, photographed from directly above, or seated in a plain white infant carrier. No other person's hands, toys, pacifiers, or support devices should appear in the frame. The background must remain uniformly white and free of patterns.
Tips for a successful children's Schengen visa photo at home:
Timing: Choose a moment when the child is awake, calm, and alert — typically after a nap or feeding.
Setup: Lay the infant on a plain white surface with soft, indirect light above; for seated older children, use the same guidance as for adults.
Expression: Encourage a calm, open-eyed neutral expression; brief vocal interactions help keep the child focused on the camera.
Background: A plain white cot sheet or a plain white wall is an ideal option.
Frame: Ensure the child's full face is visible, and no parent's hands, clothing, or accessories are in the shot.
Upload the best image to PhotoGov, and the automated tool will crop, resize, and adjust it to full Schengen compliance without any manual editing required.

sections.title: 10 Common Reasons for Schengen Visa Photo Rejection
items: Visa application centers and embassy staff reject Schengen photos more often than any other application document. Understanding the typical failure points allows you to avoid costly delays.
Incorrect dimensions: The image does not measure exactly 35 × 45 mm, or has been cropped to a non-standard aspect ratio.
Wrong background color: Background appears cream, beige, yellow-tinted, grey, or colored — only plain white or near-white is acceptable.
Shadows on face or background: Lighting from the wrong angle creates shadows under the nose, chin, or around the ears, or casts a shadow of the subject onto the background.
Non-neutral facial expression: Smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, squinting, or parted lips violate biometric standards.

Glare on the glasses in the photo/covered eyes: Though the prescription glasses are generally accepted (double-check with your country), the glare or flash reflection on the lenses is one of the most frequent rejection reasons. If you wear glasses, your eyes must be fully visible, with no glare, no frames covering your eyes, no tinted lenses, no sunglasses.
Head too small or too large: The face occupies less than 70% or more than 80% of the image height, falling outside the 32–36 mm chin-to-crown range.
Photo older than six months: The image no longer reflects the current appearance; any significant change since the photo was taken also requires a retake.
Poor print or image quality: Visible pixelation, compression artifacts, blur, or printing on standard paper rather than professional photo stock.
Digital retouching or AI enhancements: Filters, skin-smoothing, teeth whitening, background alteration that distorts the hairline, or AI face enhancements are not permitted.
Head tilted, turned, or incorrectly positioned: The face must be centered and square to the camera. Slight head tilts are a frequent and easily missed rejection cause.

sections.title: What to Do IF Your Schengen Visa Photo Gets Rejected
items: If your Schengen visa photo is rejected by the embassy or visa center, first carefully check the reason stated in the feedback slip or email, as staff usually indicate the exact problem (wrong size, incorrect background, shadows, expression, or glasses). Then retake the photo, making sure it strictly meets the official 35 × 45 mm format, head height of 32–36 mm (70–80% of the frame), plain white or very light grey background, neutral expression, and no eyewear or distracting accessories.

To avoid repeated refusals, use a professional biometric photo service or an online tool such as PhotoGov that applies the EU Visa Code and ICAO 9303 rules automatically and validates your image before you resubmit your application.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
What are the Official Schengen Visa Photo Requirements?
items: A compliant Schengen visa photo must meet the following official specifications, derived from the EU Visa Code (Regulation EC No 810/2009) and ICAO Document 9303:
Size: 35 mm wide × 45 mm high
Head height: 32–36 mm from chin to crown (70–80% of image height)
Background: Plain white or very light grey, no shadows or patterns

Recency: Taken within the last 6 months
Color: Full-color only
Glasses: Allowed, only prescription ones, frames don’t cover the eyes, no glare or flash

sections.title: What Is the Schengen Tourist Visa Photo Size?
items: The Schengen tourist visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. This is the same size used for every short-stay Schengen visa.

sections.title: What Is the Schengen Student Visa Photo Size?
items: The Schengen student visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. The photo specification does not change between visa types — a study application uses the same photo as a tourist or business application.

sections.title: What Is the Schengen Business Visa Photo Size?
items: The Schengen business visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm, with the head measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. It is identical to the size used for tourism, study, and all other short-stay Schengen visas.

sections.title: How Recent Does My Schengen Visa Photo Need to Be?
items: Your Schengen visa photo must be taken within the six months immediately preceding your application date . The image must accurately represent your current appearance. If you have undergone a significant change in appearance — including major weight change, facial surgery, or substantial change in facial hair — a new photo is required regardless of when the original was taken.

sections.title: Is the Schengen Visa Photo the Same in All 29 Member States?
items: Yes. The core specification — 35 × 45 mm size, a 32–36 mm head height, a light background, a neutral expression, and a photo no older than six months — comes from the Schengen Visa Code and ICAO Document 9303. Member states may add small procedural notes, so it is worth checking the page of the consulate or visa center you apply through.

sections.title: Is the Schengen Visa Photo Size Different from a Passport Photo?
items: For most Schengen member states, the national passport photo and the Schengen visa photo share identical dimensions (35 × 45 mm) and biometric specifications under EU and ICAO standards. In practice, a photo prepared for your German, French, Italian, or Spanish passport will meet the Schengen visa photo requirements, and vice versa. Always confirm with the specific issuing authority, as minor national variations in background shade or print format occasionally apply.

sections.title: What Background Color is Required for a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: The required background is plain white, off-white, or very light grey , uniformly lit and free of shadows, textures, gradients, or visible objects. Cream, warm beige, yellow-tinted, or mid-grey backgrounds will cause rejection. The background must be visibly lighter than the subject's face and hair to ensure adequate contrast for biometric processing.

sections.title: Are Glasses Allowed in Schengen Visa Photos?
items: Yes, but only prescription ones, with transparent lenses that don’t have glare, flash reflection, and frames that don’t cover your eyes . The eyes must be fully visible and not enlarged by the lenses (if that is your case, it’s better to take off the glasses for the photo). Prescription glasses, tinted lenses, and sunglasses are prohibited in Schengen visa photos.

sections.title: Can I Smile in a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: No. Even a slight smile is non-compliant if it changes the shape of your mouth or cheeks, or shows teeth. Keep a neutral expression, with the mouth closed, the eyes open, and the facial muscles relaxed, so the biometric measurements stay accurate.

sections.title: Are Earphones or Headphones Allowed in a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: No. Earphones, earbuds, headphones, and any other visible electronic accessories must be removed before the photo is taken.

sections.title: Is a Beard or a New Hairstyle a Problem for My Schengen Visa Photo?
items: No, as long as the photo is less than six months old and your face is fully visible. A problem arises only when facial hair or a hairstyle covers the jawline, cheeks, eyes, or eyebrows. In that case, adjust your hair or trim your beard and retake the photo.

sections.title: Do I Need to Remove Facial Piercings for a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: There is no general ban on facial piercings, but the photo is rejected if jewelry hides facial contours, casts visible shadows, or produces strong reflections. Small, matte studs usually cause no issue, while large rings or shiny metal pieces are best removed for the photo.

sections.title: Where Can I Get a Schengen Visa Photo Near Me?
items: Schengen visa photos are available at pharmacies, post offices, retail photo counters, self-service booths, and professional studios in most countries. Online photo tools are an alternative that works from any location at any time and lets you redo the photo immediately if it is not right.

sections.title: Can I Take a Schengen Visa Photo at Home?
items: Yes. A smartphone or digital camera with a resolution of at least 12 megapixels is sufficient to capture a technically acceptable image, provided the setup meets official requirements: even lighting, plain white background, neutral expression, and correct framing. The most reliable approach is to take a well-lit portrait at home and then use PhotoGov to automatically crop, resize, and validate it before submission.

sections.title: What is the Digital Schengen Visa Photo Format and Resolution?
items: For digital submission via an embassy portal, VFS Global platform, or another online system, Schengen visa photos must be submitted in JPEG (.jpg) format . The minimum recommended resolution is 413 × 531 pixels at 300 DPI (equivalent to 35 × 45 mm in print). Higher resolution — up to 600 × 771 pixels at 300 DPI — is preferred for image clarity. File size limits vary by portal but typically fall between 500 KB and 10 MB . The image must be in 24-bit sRGB color space, with no compression artifacts, filters, or digital enhancements.

sections.title: How Many Photos Do I Need for a Schengen Visa Application?
items: Most Schengen visa applications submitted at an embassy, consulate, or in-person visa application center require two identical printed photographs (35 × 45 mm). Some VFS Global and BLS International centers additionally request a single digital file for scanning and data processing. Always refer to the application instructions from the specific embassy or processing center, as requirements vary slightly between member states and application channels.

sections.title: Can Head Coverings Be Worn in Schengen Visa Photos?
items: Head coverings are permitted only for religious or medical reasons and only if they do not obscure the hairline, forehead, eyebrows, cheeks, or any part of the face. Religious head coverings (such as hijabs, turbans, or kippot) worn as a daily practice are accepted. Medical head coverings (worn due to illness or post-surgical care) are also accepted, but a signed medical certificate from a licensed practitioner may be required. Fashion hats, caps, beanies, and bandanas are not permitted under any circumstances.

sections.title: What Clothing Should I Wear for a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Wear clean, everyday clothing in solid, mid-tone, or darker colors that provide clear contrast against the white background. Avoid white, off-white, or very pale tops that blend into the background. Uniforms, military camouflage, and anything resembling official or institutional dress are prohibited. Make sure the face and neck remain clearly visible and unobstructed.

sections.title: Can I Use Makeup in My Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Yes, natural makeup is permitted provided it does not alter your facial features, skin tone, or structure in any way that would affect biometric identification. Avoid highly reflective or glittery products that may cause unwanted glare under studio or flash lighting. Heavy contouring, theatrical makeup, or face paint that changes the apparent structure of the face is not accepted. Retouching, digital skin-smoothing, and post-processing filters are prohibited.

sections.title: Are There Different Schengen Photo Requirements for Children and Infants?
items: The technical specifications — 35 × 45 mm, plain white background, 70–80% head proportion — apply to children of all ages, including infants. For babies under approximately 12 months, ICAO guidelines allow slight relaxation of the expression rule: eyes may be partially closed, and slight mouth opening is generally tolerated. The infant must be alone in the frame, with no visible parents' hands, toys, pacifiers, or support structures. Older children follow the same rules as adults.

sections.title: What Should My Child Wear for a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Dress your child in everyday clothes that contrast with the light background, such as mid-tone or darker tops without large logos or bright patterns. Avoid white tops that blend into the background, anything that looks like a uniform, and any hood, hat, or headband that covers the forehead, ears, or hairline.

sections.title: What Resolution Should My Schengen Visa Photo Have for Online Submission?
items: For digital Schengen visa photo submission, use JPEG format at 300 DPI , with pixel dimensions of at least 413 × 531 pixels (35 × 45 mm equivalent). For sharper results and compatibility with high-resolution consulate portals, 600 × 771 pixels at 300 DPI is recommended. The maximum file size is typically 10 MB , though individual portals may set lower thresholds (some VFS Global country portals specify a maximum of 1–5 MB). Color depth must be 24-bit sRGB. Do not apply any compression settings that introduce visible artifacts.

sections.title: How Do I Check If My Schengen Visa Photo Is Compliant Before Submitting?
items: Use the PhotoGov Schengen visa photo checker. Upload your image, and the automated compliance engine verifies: exact dimensions and aspect ratio, head-to-frame proportion (70–80%), background color uniformity, presence of shadows, facial expression neutrality, eye openness, and technical file quality (resolution, format, color depth). The system returns instant results indicating whether your photo meets all EU Visa Code and ICAO 9303 standards. Photos created with PhotoGov carry a compliance guarantee: if your image is rejected at the visa center due to a verifiable technical issue, customer support will provide a free retake or full refund.

sections.title: What Are the Most Common Schengen Visa Photo Rejection Reasons and How Can I Avoid Them?
items: The most frequent reasons for Schengen visa photo rejection include:
Photo dimensions outside the 35 × 45 mm standard
Background that is not plain white or very light grey
Shadows across the face, neck, or background
Wearing glasses of any kind
Non-neutral expression (smiling, squinting, raised eyebrows)
Head positioned outside the 70–80% frame proportion
Photo older than six months
Visible pixelation, blur, or poor print quality
Digital filters, retouching, or AI skin enhancement
Head tilted or turned away from the camera
To prevent rejection, create your photo with PhotoGov: the platform validates every criterion automatically and flags any non-compliance before you download the final file.

sections.title: Can I Use My Schengen Visa Photo for Another Application?
items: Yes, within reason. Because the Schengen visa photo uses the standard 35 × 45 mm biometric format, the same photo can usually be used for a European passport, an ID card, or another Schengen visa — as long as it is still within the six-month recency window and reflects your current appearance.

sections.title: Can I Use a Digital Photo for a Schengen Visa?
items: Yes. When you apply through an online appointment portal, you upload a digital photo with the application. The file must meet the 35 × 45 mm proportions, be saved as a JPEG, and stay within the portal's file-size and resolution limits.

sections.title: What Are the Schengen Visa Photo Specifications for Digital Uploads?
items: For an online Schengen visa application, the digital photo is usually a JPEG, at least 300 DPI, between 120 KB and 10 MB in file size, and up to about 1000 × 1200 pixels. The head should occupy 70–80% of the image. File limits differ between portals, so always confirm the exact figures with the consulate or visa center you are applying through.

sections.title: Can I Use a Black-and-White Photo for a Schengen Visa?
items: No. Schengen visa photos must be in color to show natural skin tones and clear detail. Black-and-white and monochrome photos are not accepted.

sections.title: How Do I Print a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Print the photo on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper, with your printer set to maximum resolution. You can print at a photo lab, a post office, a pharmacy photo counter, or at home. A resolution below 300 DPI produces a poor-quality print that is likely to be refused.

sections.title: Can I Use a Selfie for a Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Yes, if it is taken correctly. The best results come from placing the phone on a tripod or stand at eye level, using the timer or the rear camera, and producing a straight, undistorted, evenly lit portrait against a plain light background.

sections.title: Can I Edit the Background of My Schengen Visa Photo?
items: Yes. You may clean and standardize the background to a plain light tone using an online photo tool, as long as the outline of your head and face is not changed, and no visible artifacts appear around your hair. Editing that smooths skin, reshapes features, or otherwise changes your natural appearance is not allowed.

sections.title: Can Two People Use the Same Schengen Visa Photo?
items: No. Every applicant, including each child in a family application, needs their own unique, recent photo. A shared photo, or the wrong photo attached to the wrong applicant, invalidates the application.

sections.title: Singapore Passport Photo Requirements: a Complete 2026 Guide
items: A correctly taken photo is an essential part of your Singapore passport application. It must fully meet the official ICA Singapore passport photo requirements: a plain white background, 400 × 514 pixels for online submissions (at 600 DPI and up to 8 MB), or 35 × 45 mm for in‑person applications, along with several other key parameters. Even small mistakes can lead to delays or rejection.

But don't worry. This 2026 guide explains all ICA specifications. There is no need to memorise them: by using a convenient passport photo maker like PhotoGov, you can get an ICA-compliant passport photo from the comfort of your home or office. These apps usually come with features that will help you take photographs in the required dimensions. The photograph will be accepted if it complies with our photo guidelines. — The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore

sections.title: 12 Essential Singapore Passport Photo Requirements: Checklist
items: The Singapore passport picture requirements are set by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore (ICA). In turn, they are determined by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303 standards. Below is a complete list of 12 essential Singapore passport specifications. The ICA applies separate specifications to visas, and our Singapore visa photo size page prepares that format.
1. Number of Photos
One passport-size photo is required for online submission.
2. Recency
Three months . Accurately reflects the applicant's current appearance.
3. Photo Size
400 x 514 pixels — a digital photo size for an online application via e-Services in Singapore or with a form submitted from overseas. for the printed photo
4. Colour
A colour photograph , naturally reflecting the applicant's skin tone. Over- or underexposed pictures are not accepted.
5. Background
A plain white background, free from shadows, textures, or patterns, is required for ID photos in Singapore.
6. Lighting
Natural, uniform, good lighting that doesn't cast shadows or produce glare on the picture is required.
7. Positioning and Framing

Face and shoulders must be centered , square to the camera, and take about 70-80% of the frame. They must look directly into the camera. The full face, neck, and ears must be visible in the shot and unobstructed.
8. Facial Expression
Neutral facial expression with eyes open and mouth closed is acceptable. Smiling, frowning, or other similar expressions are to be avoided in Singapore ID, passport, or visa photos.
9. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories

Dress formally . Military and camouflage attire aren't allowed. Head coverings are allowed only if worn for religious reasons and don't obscure facial features. Any attire worn for medical reasons must be supported by an official confirmation letter from a medical provider.
10. Glasses

Glasses are allowed on Singapore passport photos — but only if the frame, glare, or flash reflection doesn't cover the eyes, and they remain fully visible. Tinted glasses, even prescription ones, and sunglasses aren't allowed on ID photos.
11. Print Quality
For offline submissions , the picture must be printed on high-quality photo paper with matte or semi-matte finish (glossy prints are not acceptable).
12. Digital Quality
For digital submissions via e-Services, high-resolution JPG, JPEG, HEIC, HEIF, and PNG photos are acceptable, with a maximum file size of 1-8 MB, and 400 x 514 pixel size.

sections.title: Baby Passport Photo Requirements in Singapore
items: Singaporean baby passport photos must follow the same technical specifications as adult photos: 35 mm × 45 mm for physical prints, or 400 × 514 pixels for digital submissions in JPEG format not exceeding 8 MB. The face should occupy roughly 75 percent of the frame, with approximately 3 mm from the top of the photo to the top of the hair.
Exceptions for infants:
Newborns under one month may have eyes partially or fully closed
Children under one year may keep their mouths slightly open
The baby's head can be supported from behind, provided hands remain completely out of the frame
The baby may be laid down on a white sheet instead of having them sit upright.

sections.title: Common Reasons for Singapore Passport Photo Rejection
items: Many applications get delayed or rejected due to small errors in the photo. The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority lists 10 common issues that cause rejections:
Incorrect dimensions : Photos not meeting the 35 mm × 45 mm print size or 400 × 514 pixel digital specifications​
Non-white background: Any colour, pattern, or shade violates ICA's strict plain white background requirement
Laterally inverted images : Selfies or mirror-reversed photos that flip facial features horizontally
Outdated photos : Images captured more than three months before the application
Shadows or uneven lighting : Shadows on the face, neck, or background, or overexposed/washed-out images
Incorrect facial expression : Smiling, frowning, or any non-neutral expression, rather than a closed mouth and a neutral look
Digital alterations : Any editing, filters, beauty modes, or touch-ups that modify appearance
Poor resolution or blur : Pixelated, blurry, or low-quality images not meeting sharpness standards​
Facial obstructions : Glare on glasses, hair covering eyebrows, or large reflective jewellery obscuring features
Headwear : Hats, scarves, or any other headpieces besides the religious/medical head coverings.
Using PhotoGov helps eliminate these issues automatically — the system checks each image for ICA compliance before generating your final photo.

sections.title: What to Do If Your Singapore Passport Photo is Rejected
items: If ICA rejects your passport photo, you will receive notification via letter or email explaining the specific reason for rejection. You have three options to resubmit a compliant photo:
By mail : Attach the new photo to the re-submission slip enclosed with the notification letter and mail it to ICA
Online : Use the Photo Resubmission service link (if provided in the email notification)
In person: Submit it at the Passport Unit's Information Counter, Level 2, ICA Building
Once ICA receives your new photo, processing takes approximately one to two weeks, and you will be notified when your passport is ready for collection.

sections.title: What are the Singapore Passport Photo Background Colour and Lighting Rules I Must Follow to Avoid Rejection?
items: Singapore passport photos require a plain white background with even, shadow-free lighting that leaves your face clearly visible. These are the two most common rejection triggers, so following ICA's specifications exactly will help your application proceed without delay.
Background requirements:
Colour: Pure white only. Off-white, cream, or grey backgrounds are not accepted.
Uniformity: The background must be plain with no patterns, textures, or shadows.
Coverage: The white backdrop should fill the entire frame behind your head and shoulders.
Shadows: No shadows cast by your head or body onto the background wall.
Lighting specifications:
Even illumination: Light must fall uniformly across your face without creating hotspots or dark areas.
No shadows: Shadows under the chin, nose, or around the eyes will cause rejection.
No red-eye: Camera flash should not produce red-eye effect; retouched red-eye removal is not permitted.
Natural appearance: Avoid overexposure that washes out skin tones or underexposure that makes the image too dark.
Common mistakes to avoid:
Using a cream or off-white wall instead of pure white.
Taking photos near windows that create uneven side-lighting or shadows.
Using a flash too close to the face, creating harsh shadows or glare on glasses.
Standing too far from the background, allowing shadows to appear behind you.
If you are taking the photo at home, position yourself about 1 metre away from a plain white wall and use natural daylight or two balanced light sources at 45-degree angles to eliminate shadows.

sections.title: What Are the Guidelines for Clothing, Glasses, and Head Coverings in Singapore Passport Photo Requirements?
items: Clothing . Wear everyday attire that contrasts with the white background. Avoid uniforms, costumes, or clothing that matches the background colour. Formal or business casual clothing is recommended for official documents.

Glasses . Remove glasses if possible. If you must wear them for medical reasons, ensure the lenses are clear and untinted with no glare or reflection. Frames must not cover any part of the eyes. Sunglasses and tinted lenses are prohibited.

Head Coverings . Hats and head coverings are generally not allowed. Exceptions apply for religious or medical reasons only if supported by a signed statement from a religious leader or doctor. The head covering must be dark-coloured to contrast with the white background, and your full face must remain visible from chin to forehead without any shadows cast on your face.

sections.title: What Are the Common Reasons Singapore Passport Photos Get Rejected, and How Do I Make Sure Mine Meets All Requirements?
items: ICA rejects passport photos that fail to meet strict technical and content standards. The most frequent reasons for rejection are easily avoidable with attention to detail.
Common reasons for rejection:
Non-white background: Off-white, cream, grey, or patterned backgrounds are not accepted. Only pure white is permitted.
Laterally inverted images: Selfies or mirror-reversed photos that flip facial features horizontally will be rejected.
Outdated photos: Images taken more than three months before the application.
Shadows or uneven lighting: Shadows on the face, neck, or background, or uneven brightness across the face.
Digital alterations: Any editing, filters, beauty modes, or touch-ups that modify appearance.

Facial obstructions: Glare on glasses, hair covering eyebrows, or large reflective jewellery obscuring features.
How to ensure your photo meets requirements:
Use a plain white wall as the backdrop and position yourself about one metre away to avoid shadows.
Ensure even lighting from the front without harsh shadows or red-eye.
Take the photo within three months of your application date.
Face the camera directly with a neutral expression and mouth closed.
Avoid any digital editing or filters; submit the original image.
Verify dimensions: 35 mm × 45 mm for prints or 400 × 514 pixels for digital uploads.
Remove glasses if possible, and keep hair away from your face.

sections.title: Are There Different Singapore Passport Photo Requirements for Children and Infants, and What Should Parents Prepare?
items: No, the technical specifications remain identical for applicants of all ages. Children and infants must submit photos measuring 35 mm × 45 mm for prints or 400 × 514 pixels for digital submissions, with the same white background and lighting requirements as adults.
However, there are a few less strict rules for younger children:
Newborns under one month : Eyes do not need to be fully open.
Infants : May be photographed lying on a white sheet instead of sitting upright.
Support : Parents may support the baby's head, but hands must not be visible in the final photo.
Expression : Neutral expression is preferred, but mouths may be slightly open for children under one year.​
Prohibited items : No toys, pacifiers, bottles, or other objects may appear in the photograph.

items: Below is a list of 11 essential Singapore passport photo requirements for digital photo uploads to ICA E Services.

Lighting : Even illumination with no shadows on face or background
Face size : the face must occupy 70-80% of the photo height
Position : Full face, front view, centred in the frame
Expression : Neutral with no smile, mouth closed, and eyes open.
Additional rules:
No headgear unless worn for religious or medical reasons (must not cover facial features)
Glasses permitted only if eyes are clearly visible with no glare or reflection; no tinted lenses
No digital editing, filters, or alterations to the original image​
Scanned prints are not accepted; must be original digital capture.

sections.title: Can I Smile In A Singapore Passport Photo?
items: No. You must keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed and eyes fully open. Broad smiles, visible teeth, or exaggerated expressions are not allowed because they change how your face looks and can lead to rejection.​

sections.title: Are Glasses Allowed In A Singapore Passport Photo?
items: Yes, but only if they do not obstruct your eyes. The frames must not cover the pupils, there should be no glare or reflections on the lenses, and the lenses cannot be tinted; sunglasses and dark prescription lenses are never permitted.​

sections.title: Can I Wear A Headscarf, Turban, Or Other Head Covering?
items: Yes, when it is worn for religious or medical reasons. The covering must not hide any part of your face from chin to forehead and should not cast heavy shadows or obscure your features.​

sections.title: Singapore Visa Photo Requirements in 2026: Complete Guide

sections.title: 11 Essential Singapore Passport Photo Requirements: Checklist
items: The Singapore visa photo requirements are defined by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore (ICA) and follow the biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO). We created this Checklist with 12 passport photo requirements to help you smooth the application process and produce an acceptable photo on the first try. Requirement

1. Number of Photos
One visa photo is required for online applications. Visa centres may require 1-2 identical prints (check your provider's instructions).
2. Recency
The picture must be taken within the past three months and reflect the applicant's current appearance. A new photo must be submitted for each application; previously used photos are not accepted.
3. Photo Size
35×45 mm (1.38×1.77 inches) for printed photos; 400×514 pixels for online photo submission through e‑Services or overseas missions. The applicant's head must occupy 70-80% of the frame (25-35 mm).
4. Colour

A colour photograph with natural skin tone and accurate exposure is required. The photo must be clear, in focus, and free from any reflections or shadows. Overexposed or underexposed images are rejected.

The applicant's face and shoulders must be centered in the frame. Eyes directed at the camera, with the full face, neck, and ears visible.

A neutral facial expression with both eyes open, and the mouth closed, looking directly into the camera. Smiling or frowning is not permitted.

Appropriate everyday attire in darker colours is required. Head coverings are permitted only for medical, religious, or racial purposes — and only if they don't obscure facial features. Hair should not cover the face or eyes. Uniforms are not allowed in visa photos.

Incorrect background colour : Background that is off-white, cream, coloured, patterned, or textured instead of a plain white backdrop without shadows.
Outdated photos : Images taken longer than 3 months ago or no longer matching your current appearance (for example, after major changes to facial hair or hairstyle).
Shadows or uneven lighting : Visible shadows on the face, neck, or background, or strong highlights that wash out facial features.
Wrong facial expression : Smiling broadly, frowning, tilting the head, or not looking straight at the camera instead of a neutral, front-facing pose with eyes open and mouth closed.
Digital retouching and filters : Beauty modes, skin-smoothing, colour filters, red-eye correction, or any edits that alter natural appearance.
Blur, noise, or low resolution : Grainy, pixelated, out-of-focus, or low-quality images that don't show clear facial detail. Digital files with low resolution (below 300 DPI) or larger than 8 MB.
Obstructions on the face : Hair covering eyes or eyebrows, heavy glare on glasses, tinted lenses, or large jewellery hiding facial contours.
Head coverings and accessories : Fashion hats, caps, or non-religious/non-medical headwear that conceals the hairline or casts shadows. Religious headwear must not obscure facial features.

Poor print quality : Home inkjet prints, streaks, colour casts, creases, fingerprints, or damage to the photo surface. Incorrect paper type (glossy instead of matte or semi-matte) or photos with white borders.

requirements/us-visa-photo-requirements.h1: Learn the 2026 US Visa Photo Requirements: Expert-Checked & Verified

sections.title: Learn the 2026 US Visa Photo Requirements: Expert-Checked & Verified
Learn the 2026 US Visa Photo Requirements: Expert-Checked & Verified
items: The U.S. has some of the strictest visa photo requirements in the world: even a small deviation from the rules can lead to an instant rejection. To avoid delays, your picture must follow every specification — a square aspect ratio, printed size of 2 x 2 inches with the head measuring 1 to 1 3/8 inches, a digital file between 600 x 600 and 1,200 x 1,200 pixels, a plain white or off‑white background, no glasses, taken within the last six months, and be compliant with all other technical parameters. Our US visa photo tool helps you crop and size your picture for the selected document.
This Complete 2026 Guide covers all U.S. visa photo requirements you need to keep in mind to prepare a compliant image that is accepted on the first try. Follow them, and enjoy your trip to the U.S.!
Source: U.S. Department of State

sections.title: 12 Essential US Visa Photo Requirements
items: The U.S. Department of State sets detailed requirements for its immigrant and non-immigrant visa photos, covering every aspect from the size and background to the number of images, their recency, and submission channels. In addition to key national rules, U.S. visa photos must follow the official biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303. To save you time and effort, we gathered all official requirements in this guide — with every single one manually checked and verified by our U.S. ID photo compliance team. Crew members use the same square format, prepared on our 2x2 inch USA crew visa photo page.
Parameter
Requirement
1. Number of photos

One digital photo is required for applicants submitting the DS‑160 or DS‑1648 online forms or applying for a Diversity visa . Two printed photos are required for the green card interview, Form DS‑260 .
2. Recency

The visa photo must be taken within the last 6 months and clearly show the applicant's current appearance and normal aging process. Individuals who have undergone a significant change in appearance, like weight loss, must provide a new photo that reflects this change.
3. US visa photo size

Square aspect ratio — for printed photos, 2×2 inches (51×51 mm) . The head centered, and the face measured between 1–1 3/8 inches (25–35 mm); for digital photos, 600 x 600 to 1,200 x 1,200 pixels with the head covering 50–69% of the image height.
4. Background
A plain white or off‑white background without patterns or textures.
5. Lighting
Even lighting . The image must be clear and show the applicant's natural skin tone, with no shadows or reflections on the face or background.
6. Facial expression and positioning
The applicant is facing the camera directly, with a neutral facial expression , eyes open, and mouth closed.
7. Clothing
Everyday clothes in colors that contrast with a white background . No camouflage attire or uniforms are permitted. Religious clothing worn daily is allowed, but the full face must be visible.
8. Head covering and accessories / Hearing devices

An applicant cannot wear a hat or a head covering that obscures facial features or the hairline, unless it's worn daily for religious or medical reasons . Headphones and wireless hands‑free devices are not permitted. If a US visa applicant normally wears a hearing aid or similar device, they may keep it in the ID photos.
9. Eyeglasses

Glasses are not allowed , except for rare medical reasons such as recent eye surgery. In these cases, a signed doctor's statement is required. If accepted, the frames must not cover the eyes, and the image must be free of glare, shadows, or lens refraction.
10. Facial surgery
When an applicant has undergone a facial surgery that has significantly changed their appearance, a signed doctor's statement verifying the identity is required.
11. Print quality

The photo must be printed in color on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper at 600 DPI , a square aspect ratio exactly 2 x 2 inches, without visible borders, frames, or other artefacts. It has to be sharp, well‑focused, free from pixels, dots, or compression artefacts.
12. Digital quality
Digital file must be 600 × 600 to 1,200 x 1,200 pixels , saved as a JPEG, 24-bit color (sRGB), 240 KB max.

sections.title: Acceptable US Visa Photos
Unacceptable US Visa Photos
US Visa Photos for Special Cases — from Religious Clothing to Appearance Change
items: Below are detailed explanations for different “appearance cases” — and what to do when taking a US visa photo if you have one of them.

Hijab, headscarf, kippah, turban. Religious head coverings worn daily are permitted, provided the full face is visible from the bottom of the chin to the top of the forehead, and from edge to edge of the face. The covering must not cast shadows on the face. A signed statement attesting to daily religious wear is not formally required, but some consulates request one — keep one prepared if you regularly wear religious attire.
Niqab and full-face veils. Permitted only when the veil is parted or removed enough to fully expose the face. The photo cannot show only the eyes.
Hearing aids. Hearing aids, cochlear implants, and similar medical devices may be worn in the photo. Wireless or Bluetooth hearing devices that look like consumer earbuds aren’t allowed.

Prosthetic eyes / Eye patches. Permitted, but the photo should clearly show your normal everyday appearance. If you wear a patch only some of the time, use the version that matches your travel documents. A medical statement is required. Wheelchair users and applicants who cannot sit upright. The US Department of State allows photos taken in any position the applicant is able to maintain, provided the head is straight and facing the camera. A plain white backdrop behind the applicant must be used— a white sheet held up by a helper works well.

Elderly applicants and applicants with health conditions. Eyes that are partially open due to medical conditions (Bell's palsy, ptosis, recent surgery) are evaluated on a case-by-case basis. A signed letter from a treating physician explaining the condition will reduce the chance of rejection.
Applicants with significant facial surgery or scarring. A signed doctor's statement verifying identity is required. The photo must reflect current appearance — do not submit a pre-surgery photo.

Printed photos are required for immigrant visa interviews (Form DS-260) and brought to the embassy on the day of the appointment.

sections.title: US Visa Photo Requirements by Visa Type
items: All non-immigrant U.S. visa categories — B1/B2, F-1, M-1, J-1, H-1B, L-1, L-2, O-1, O-2, K-1, and others — use the same DS-160 photo standards described in the requirements table above: square 2 × 2 inches, white or off-white background, taken within the last 6 months, no glasses, neutral expression. Below are the category-specific nuances applicants should be aware of.

sections.title: F-1 / M-1 Student Visa Photo
items: Take the photo close to your SEVIS appointment date — not before — so it reflects your most recent appearance for the school's I-20 records and the consular interview.

sections.title: J-1 Exchange Visitor Visa Photo
items: Some J-1 program sponsors (au pair, intern, summer-work-travel) require a separate ID photo in their internal portal. These sponsor photos are usually less strict than DS-160 standards, but using a compliant DS-160 photo for both is the safest choice.

sections.title: K-1 Fiancé(e) Visa Photo
items: In addition to the DS-160 photo, the U.S. citizen petitioner files Form I-129F, which requires two passport-style printed photos of both the petitioner and the beneficiary, taken within the last 30 days. These I-129F photos must meet USCIS passport-photo standards (essentially identical to the State Department visa standards).

sections.title: L-1 Intracompany Transferee Visa Photo
items: L-2 dependents (spouse and children) each need their own individual photo — one photo per applicant, regardless of age. Family group shots are never accepted.

sections.title: O-1 / O-2 Extraordinary Ability Visa Photo
items: O-1 applicants frequently submit professional headshots from media kits — almost always non-compliant. Backgrounds, lighting, and stylized expressions used in promotional photography violate U.S. visa standards. Take a dedicated visa photo, not a marketing portrait.

sections.title: Diversity Visa (DV Lottery) Photo
items: The DV Lottery has the strictest photo verification of any U.S. visa program. Reusing a previous DV Lottery photo — even a fully compliant one — results in automatic disqualification, since the State Department uses facial-recognition software to detect duplicate entries across years. See our DV Lottery photo tool for a step-by-step compliance check.

sections.title: Immigrant Visa Photo (IR, CR, EB, F-Categories)
items: Immigrant visa applicants file Form DS-260 online and must bring two printed 2 × 2-inch photos to the consular interview. Both prints must be identical, on glossy or matte photo paper, in color, and taken within the last 6 months. Some embassies request additional photos for the medical examination — check your appointment instructions.

sections.title: US Green Card Photo: Forms I-485, I-130, I-765, I-131, N-400
items: Green card applicants frequently confuse U.S. visa photo rules (set by the Department of State, used at consulates abroad) with U.S. immigration photo rules (set by USCIS, used inside the United States). The standards are nearly identical — but a few key differences matter.
Form
Purpose
Photos Required
Submitted How

Mailed with application; biometrics taken later at ASC

2 identical color prints of beneficiary, 2 × 2 inches
Mailed with the petition

Mailed with the application

Mailed with the application

Mailed with the application

USCIS specifies that photos should be taken within the last 30 days (stricter than the State Department's 6-month rule), printed on thin paper, with the applicant's name and A-number written lightly in pencil on the back. Always write your name on both prints — USCIS officers process millions of forms a year, and unidentified photos can be lost from your file.

For a green card interview, you must provide two identical color prints measuring exactly 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm) on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper, with the head sized 1–1 3/8 inches (25–35 mm) from chin to crown — covering 50–69% of the image height. The prints must be taken within the last 6 months, sharp and in focus, on a plain white or off-white background, with a neutral expression, mouth closed, and eyes open and clearly visible. Digital retouching, beauty filters, and uniforms are not permitted.

sections.title: ESTA Photo Requirements
items: The Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) is the online pre-clearance system for citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries. ESTA itself does not require you to upload a photo at the application stage — applicants enter only passport, biographical, and travel data. However, the photo embedded in your machine-readable passport ( the "biometric chip" photo ) is the one U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers compare to your face when you arrive.

For this reason, your passport photo must already meet ICAO Document 9303 biometric standards: square or rectangular, plain light background, neutral expression, no glasses, taken within the last 6 months of your passport application. If your passport is more than 5 years old, or if you've had a facial surgery that has significantly changed your looks, weight changes, or aging since your last passport photo, U.S. CBP may pull you aside for secondary inspection. Renewing your passport with a fresh, compliant photo is the safest approach.

sections.title: How to Apply for a Nonimmigrant US Visa?
items: To apply for a US visa, you must complete the DS-160 form online and prepare official documents — your valid passport, confirmation page, and fee receipt. A suitable photo that meets the US visa photo requirements must be uploaded during the application. When reviewing your case, a Department of State employee will check that your photo meets the standards and that all paperwork is correct. The next step is to schedule an interview at the US embassy or consulate where you apply, depending on your location. Different visa categories (for example, B1/B2 visitor visas, student visas, or work visas) may require additional supporting documents.

sections.title: Step-by-Step: How to Upload Your Photo to DS-160
items: The CEAC online application (Consular Electronic Application Center) is where you upload your photo for the DS-160 form. The interface is notoriously strict — even compliant photos are sometimes rejected by the automated check. Here's how to navigate it.

Step 1. Prepare your photo file. Make sure it is JPEG (.jpg), square, between 600 × 600 and 1200 × 1200 pixels, and between 54 KB and 240 KB. PhotoGov produces a file ready for direct upload — no resizing needed.
Step 2. Log in to the CEAC with your DS-160 application ID.
Step 3. Navigate to the "Upload Photo" page. You will see two options: "Upload Photo" and "I will provide a photo at the time of the interview."
Step 4. Click "Upload Photo" and select your file. The system will run an automated check. If accepted, you'll see a green checkmark. If rejected, you'll see one of the following error codes:
Head not centered / head out of frame: Recrop with the head centered and the face occupying 50–69% of image height.
Background not uniform: Retake with a plain white wall, no shadows, no objects.
Pixel dimensions out of range: Resize to 600 × 600 to 1200 × 1200 pixels.
File size too large / too small: Re-export the JPEG between 54 KB and 240 KB.
Color depth incorrect: Re-save as 24-bit color JPEG (not grayscale, not 8-bit).
Glasses detected: Retake without eyeglasses.
Face not detected: Retake with proper lighting and the head facing forward.
Multiple faces detected: Make sure only the applicant is in frame.
Step 5. If the upload fails three times, choose the second option ("I will provide a photo at the time of interview") and bring two printed 2 × 2 photos to your interview.
Step 6. After a successful upload, save your DS-160 confirmation page. The barcode and photo thumbnail must be visible — print this page and bring it to your interview.

sections.title: Why US Visa Photos Get Rejected — and What to Do About It
items: According to data published by the U.S. Department of State and consular post reports, roughly one in four visa photos uploaded to the DS-160 application is flagged as non-compliant. Photos rejected at the embassy interview itself can delay your case by weeks. Understanding why photos are rejected — and how to recover — is the single fastest way to make sure your application is approved on the first try.

sections.title: The 12 Most Common Rejection Reasons
items: The background is not white or off-white. Cream, beige, light gray, light blue, and patterned walls are the number-one reason photos are rejected. The background must be uniform, plain, and clearly white or off-white — without textures, shadows, gradients, or visible objects.

Shadows on the face or background. Side lighting, overhead lighting, and direct sunlight all create shadows that the State Department's facial recognition system reads as facial deformities. Use indirect, even, front-facing daylight from a window.
The head is the wrong size. The head from chin to crown must measure 1 to 1 3/8 inches (25–35 mm), or 50–69% of the image height. Heads that are too small or too large are an instant rejection.

Glasses. Eyeglasses have not been allowed in U.S. visa photos since November 1, 2016. Even if you wear them every day, you must remove them. The only exception is a documented medical reason (e.g., recent eye surgery) accompanied by a signed statement from a medical professional.

Smiling or showing teeth. Your expression must be neutral, with your mouth closed. A natural, slight upward curve at the corners of the mouth is acceptable; anything more — including a closed-lip smile that lifts the cheeks — risks rejection.
Eyes closed, partially closed, or looking off-camera. Both eyes must be fully open and looking directly into the lens. This is the single most common reason baby visa photos are rejected.

The photo is older than 6 months, or the appearance has changed significantly. Even if you haven't aged a day, a photo more than 6 months old will be rejected. The same applies if your appearance has changed (weight, beard, hair color, tattoos visible on the face).
Hair covering the face. Hair must not fall over the eyes, and both edges of the face should be visible. Ears do not have to be visible, but the face cannot be obscured.

Filters, beauty modes, or AI retouching. iPhone Portrait Mode, Snapchat-style filters, skin-smoothing apps, and any kind of background blur are all grounds for rejection. AI-generated and AI-edited images are detected and rejected since 2024 — the photo must be unedited.

Wrong file format or pixel size. Files must be JPEG, square (1:1), between 600×600 and 1200×1200 pixels, and 54 KB–240 KB. Files outside this range are rejected by the CEAC upload tool before you even submit.

Uniforms, camouflage, or clothing that blends with the background. Military, police, hospital, and airline uniforms are not allowed. White shirts that merge with the white backdrop are also a frequent cause of rejection.
Headphones, AirPods, or visible Bluetooth devices. Bluetooth earpieces and consumer audio devices are not allowed. Medical hearing aids are permitted.

sections.title: What to Do If Your US Visa Photo is Rejected
items: A photo rejection is almost never a final decision. Here's how to recover.

Step 1. Identify the exact rejection reason. If your photo was rejected at the CEAC upload stage (DS-160), you'll see a specific error code on screen — see the full error-code list in the DS-160 upload step-by-step section below. If your photo was rejected at the embassy interview, the consular officer will tell you verbally.
Step 2. Map the error to one of the 12 requirements above and identify the specific rule you violated.

Step 3. Retake the photo from scratch. Don't try to edit or "fix" the rejected photo — Photoshopped visa photos are detectable by the State Department's verification systems and can lead to a permanent ban for misrepresentation. Take a new photo from scratch, following the corrected requirement.

Step 4. Re-upload (DS-160) or re-print (DS-260). For DS-160, return to your CEAC application and re-upload the new file. For DS-260 / immigrant visa interviews, bring two new prints to the rescheduled interview.

Step 5. If rejected at the embassy interview, request the rescheduling instructions. Most consulates will allow you to return with a compliant photo within a few days, sometimes the same day. Some embassies even have on-site photo services, though their quality varies.

Step 6. If your application is delayed because of repeated photo rejections, contact the embassy directly. Each U.S. embassy and consulate has its own contact channel — you can find yours on usembassy.gov .

To minimize rejection risk, run your photo through an automated compliance checker before uploading. Tools like PhotoGov verify all 12 requirements (background, head size, shadows, expression, etc.) in under 30 seconds and flag issues before you submit.

sections.title: Where to Take a US Visa Photo (and How Much it Costs)
items: A compliant photo is a vital part of your visa application — getting it right the first time saves money and weeks of delay. Below are the four main options, with realistic 2026 pricing and rejection risk.

Online visa photo editor. Upload a photo from your iPhone or digital camera; the service automatically crops it to U.S. visa standards and returns a digital file or printable PDF in under 30 seconds. The fastest, cheapest, and most reliable approach when you have a decent original shot.

Pharmacies, shipping centers, and post offices (CVS, Walgreens, FedEx Office, UPS Store, USPS). Convenient locations and trained staff, but quality varies by store, and the wait depends on staff availability. Searching "US visa photo near me" usually returns these first.

Professional photographer or studio. The most reliable in-person option. A photographer handles lighting and composition, and a high-quality printer is on-site. Most expensive and requires an appointment.
Photo booth. The cheapest option, but the least reliable. Vending-machine booths often produce photos with glare, shadows, or wrong backgrounds — frequently rejected at U.S. embassies.
